_readme: Firsts with Sam: until a lady has crossed a line with Sam, private time with him only offers services up to that point (services.json → tier: 1 kissing & touching, 2 hands & mouth, 3 everything). Clients aren't affected.
stages: the three lines. label shows on her sheet; situation is passed to the AI writer for that first.

paces: trust she needs for stage 1/2/3, and gap = weeks between her firsts. pentTrust: how much less trust a lady at max lust needs (she pushes past her own pace). holdWeeks: how long she waits after Sam says 'not yet'.

chance: odds per week that a ready lady's first happens on its own (pent = she's at max lust; init = she makes the first move; week = everyone else). It can also happen at the end of a good date, or from 'Take the next step' on her sheet.

characters.<key>: pace (fast/normal/slow), path (the stages her firsts reach, in order: [1,2,3], [1,3], [2,3] or [3]), init (makes the move herself), events keyed by stage, and optionally pent keyed by stage for when she can't wait. Guests from guests.json can be added here too, by key.

Event: title, text (the setup), image {comp, setting, sam, pov, towel} (a picture for this moment), go / goRes (crossing the line; then the service's own line and her reaction follow), wait / waitRes (Sam says not yet), optional act (which service to show; must be at that stage), optional situation (AI prompt context). {name} = her name.

templates: for ladies without their own. Keys 1, 2, 3, jump (from nothing straight past a first kiss), and pent_<key> versions. Optional pers / traits / race lists narrow a variant to matching ladies (they're picked more often when they match).
roll: how pace / path / init are rolled for ladies without their own (generic ladies at random; guests seeded by key so they're the same every game). mods by trait or personality add weight.
relaxed: the bath / walk-in beats of partner stories once she and Sam have reached stage relaxedAt: no more embarrassment. Choices use the arc effect schema (t/m/l, res with {N}).

lewdEase: lewdness eases the trust gate for her firsts. Trust needed for a stage drops by per x (lewd - from), at most max (live: uses her current lewdness; firstNeed() in firsts.js; combines with pentTrust).
roll.lewdPath: when a generic lady's lewdness is at least 'at' as her firsts are rolled, these weights are added to the path odds (on top of the existing lewd >= 60 fast / < 20 slow pace nudge).

templates: a variant may carry lewdMin (0-100): it only applies to ladies with lewdness >= lewdMin, and counts as a matching variant (picked more often). Variants without lewdMin stay usable for everyone.

characters.<key>.events.jump (optional): her own scene for going straight from nothing past a first kiss; used instead of her stage scene when she has no firsts yet. Guests can have events without pace/path/init (those stay rolled).

1.label: First kiss
1.situation: This is their very first kiss; it stays at kissing and touching.

2.label: Going further
2.situation: This is the first time they've gone further than kissing, though not all the way.

3.label: First night
3.situation: This is their first night together.

defaults.waitRes: {name} nods. She doesn't seem upset. If anything, she looks like she's already planning the next time.

text: Sam opens the washroom door and finds {name} in the tub. She doesn't so much as reach for a towel. "Close the door," she says. "From the inside."
{name} is soaking in the bath when Sam walks in by mistake. She just smiles and shifts over to make room.

choices.label: Join her
choices.res: The water's perfect. {N} says so, several times.

text: {name} walks into the washroom while Sam's in the tub, doesn't even pause, and sits on the edge with her feet in the water. "Scoot over."
{name} wanders in while Sam's bathing, hands him a towel he didn't ask for, and stays to chat like it's the most natural thing in the world. For them, it is.

choices.label: Scoot over
choices.res: There isn't really room for two. They make it work.

choices.label: "Some privacy?"
choices.res: {N} laughs, kisses the top of his head, and leaves him to it.

1.title: {name}: A Quiet Moment
1.text: Sam walks {name} back to her room after a long shift. At her door she stops, turns, and just looks at him for a moment, like she's deciding something.

image.comp: standing at her bedroom door, turned toward him, looking up at him with a soft hesitant smile
image.setting: lantern-lit upstairs hallway at night

1.goRes: She meets him halfway. It's brief, and then it isn't.
1.waitRes: {name} smiles, a little disappointed, a little relieved. "Goodnight, Sam."

1.title: {name}: Under the Eaves
1.text: A sudden downpour traps Sam and {name} under the eaves out back. She's laughing, soaked, shoulder to shoulder with him, and then she isn't laughing anymore.

image.comp: sheltering under wooden eaves in the rain beside him, soaked and laughing, leaning closer
image.setting: back alley in heavy rain, lantern light, wet cobbles

1.goRes: The rain doesn't stop. They don't notice.
1.wait: Make a run for the door
1.waitRes: They sprint inside, dripping. {name} keeps glancing at him all evening.

1.title: {name}: Bold Move
1.text: {name} plants herself in front of Sam in the hallway. "I'm going to kiss you now," she announces. "Objections?"

image.comp: blocking a hallway with hands on her hips, confident flirtatious grin, leaning toward him
image.setting: lantern-lit hallway of a pleasure house

1.goRes: "Good," she says, and does. Thoroughly.
1.waitRes: "Overruled. Later." She winks and saunters off.

1.title: {name}: Very Brave
1.text: {name} has been hovering near Sam all evening. Finally she tugs his sleeve, closes her eyes, and goes up on her toes, shaking a little.

image.comp: on tiptoe with eyes squeezed shut, tugging his sleeve, deeply blushing, trembling slightly
image.setting: quiet corner of a lantern-lit lounge

1.goRes: It's barely a kiss. She looks like she might float away.
1.waitRes: She opens her eyes, mortified, then relieved. "...Thank you. Next time. Maybe."

1.title: {name}: A Gift for You
1.text: {name} hands Sam a small wrapped package. While he fumbles with the ribbon she leans in and kisses his cheek. Then, considering, not his cheek.

image.comp: leaning in to kiss him as he unwraps a small gift, playful sly smile
image.setting: cozy lounge, warm lantern light

1.goRes: The gift is a bookmark. He doesn't find out until much later.
1.waitRes: "Open it, then." She laughs and leaves him to it.

1.title: {name}: Elegant Timing
1.text: {name} chooses her moment carefully: a balcony, a view, the last light of evening. "I prefer not to leave these things to chance," she says.

image.comp: on a balcony at sunset, turning toward him with calm poise, one hand on the railing
image.setting: balcony overlooking a fantasy town at sunset

1.goRes: It's exactly as composed and lovely as she planned. Then less composed.
1.waitRes: "Of course." She inclines her head, entirely unruffled. "There will be other sunsets."

1.title: {name}: Off the Clock
1.text: {name} has spent the night smiling at strangers. Afterward she finds Sam in the kitchen and sits down across from him, chin in her hand. "You know what's strange?" she says. "I've lost count of the men I've kissed this month. And I'm nervous."

image.comp: sitting across a small kitchen table late at night, chin in her hand, looking at him with a nervous, unguarded smile
image.setting: house kitchen after closing, a single lantern, two cups of tea

1.goRes: It's nothing like work. She seems as surprised by that as he is.
1.waitRes: {name} laughs, relieved and a little disappointed. "Nobody's ever said that to me before."

1.title: {name}: Lantern Duty
1.text: Closing time, and {name} has asked Sam to help her put out the lanterns along the front walk. One by one the lights go dark, and the street grows quiet and blue. At the last lantern she stops with her hand on the glass. "I always leave this one for last," she says. "It gives me an excuse to stand next to you."

image.comp: standing beside a hanging lantern, hand on the glass, looking up at him with a shy warm smile
image.setting: front walk of the house at night, lanterns half out, blue dusk

1.goRes: She turns her face up, and the last lantern goes out on its own, or maybe neither of them was looking.
1.waitRes: {name} laughs under her breath and hooks her arm through his. "Next lantern, then."

1.title: {name}: Flour on Her Cheek
1.text: {name} is up to her elbows in bread dough in the kitchen at dawn, and there is flour on her cheek, her nose and one eyebrow. Sam reaches out to brush it off. Her breath catches. "You missed a spot," she whispers, though he hasn't missed any, and she is looking at his mouth.

image.comp: close to him at a kitchen worktable, flour on her cheek, looking at his mouth, hands covered in dough
image.setting: warm house kitchen at dawn, flour dust in the light

1.goRes: She leaves two floury handprints on his hoodie, and neither of them cares.
1.waitRes: She lets him wipe her cheek, blushing furiously, and pretends not to be disappointed. The bread, unattended, is slightly burned.

1.title: {name}: Rooftop Stars
1.text: {name} has dragged a blanket up to the roof, the only place in the house where the noise can't follow. The tiles are still warm from the day, the stars very sharp. She pats the spot next to her. When Sam sits, she leans her head on his shoulder, then tips her chin up. "Just checking something," she says.

image.comp: sitting on a rooftop blanket under the stars, head on his shoulder, tipping her chin up to him
image.setting: rooftop of the house at night, warm tiles, bright stars

1.goRes: She was checking. It checks out. She says so, twice.
1.waitRes: "That one's the Cup," she says, a little hoarse, and keeps her head on his shoulder anyway.

1.title: {name}: Mending
1.text: Sam's hoodie has a torn cuff, and {name} takes it from him without a word and sits in the lamp-glow with her needle and thread. The room is hushed. When she bites off the thread, she looks up, holds the sleeve out, and doesn't let go of it when he takes hold. "All fixed," she says softly. "But I'm not done."

image.comp: sitting in lamplight with a needle and thread, holding the sleeve of his hoodie, looking up at him through her lashes
image.setting: quiet sewing corner by the lamp, evening, baskets of thread

1.goRes: She pulls him down by the repaired sleeve. The stitching holds beautifully.
1.waitRes: "Anytime," she says, and finishes the sleeve with a very satisfied little smile, as if she already has a plan.

1.title: {name}: Winner Takes
1.text: {name} has beaten Sam at cards for the fourth night in a row. "You owe me a stake," she says, collecting the coins, then leaving them where they lie. She leans over the table until the candle flickers. "Unless you'd like to pay in another way."

image.comp: leaning across a card table toward him, a hand of cards held up, sly confident smile
image.setting: common room card table at night, candle, scattered coins

1.goRes: The candle goes out. Nobody relights it.
1.waitRes: "Oh, I like that." She shuffles slowly, eyes on him. "I'll collect next time."

2.title: {name}: Further
2.text: {name} pulls Sam into her room after a long day and closes the door. "I've been thinking about more than kissing," she admits. "A lot more."

image.comp: leaning back against a closed door in a dim bedroom, pulling him close by his hoodie, heated eyes
image.setting: small cozy bedroom at night, one candle

2.goRes: She has, in fact, been thinking about it a lot.
2.waitRes: "It is." She kisses him once more, slowly. "Next time, though."

2.title: {name}: Late Night
2.text: Sam can't sleep. Neither can {name}, apparently; she's sitting on the end of his bed when he looks up. "I had an idea," she says.

image.comp: sitting on the end of a bed in the dark, leaning toward him with a sly smile, candle beside her
image.setting: his bedroom late at night, one candle

2.goRes: She doesn't tell him. She demonstrates.
2.waitRes: "Boring." She tucks the blanket around him and leaves him wide awake.

2.title: {name}: Curious
2.text: {name} has questions. Very specific questions. She asks them in a rush, red to the ears, and then: "Could you... show me?"

image.comp: sitting on a bed hugging a pillow, red to the ears, curious earnest eyes on him
image.setting: quiet bedroom, afternoon light through curtains

2.goRes: She's a very attentive student.
2.waitRes: "Right. Yes." She buries her face in the pillow.

2.title: {name}: Not Done Yet
2.text: {name} stops Sam mid-kiss. "I'm not done," she says, and pushes him back onto the sofa.

image.comp: pushing him back onto a lounge sofa, standing over him with a challenging grin
image.setting: empty lounge after hours, low lanterns

2.goRes: She keeps going.
2.waitRes: "Coward." She laughs and drags him upstairs instead... to say goodnight. Pointedly.

2.title: {name}: Not Like Work
2.text: "I know how to do this," {name} says, her hands at Sam's collar. "I'm very good at it. That's the problem." She stops. "With you I don't want to be good at it. I just want it to be us."

image.comp: standing close in her room, her hands resting on his collar, hesitating, eyes searching his face
image.setting: her bedroom at night, soft lamplight, the door closed

2.goRes: She stops performing halfway through, starts laughing, and doesn't let go of him.
2.waitRes: "Okay," says {name}, and means it. She keeps her hands on his collar a while longer anyway.

2.title: {name}: Warm Hands
2.text: It is a cold night, and {name} has brought Sam a hot cup of spiced wine, which she then sets aside. She takes his hands in hers and rubs the warmth back into them, slowly, thumb by thumb. Her eyes stay on his face. "Your hands are always cold," she says. "I'd like to know where else."

image.comp: holding both of his hands between hers by the fireplace, rubbing them warm, heated look
image.setting: small parlor with a crackling fire, winter night

2.goRes: She finds out thoroughly, and keeps his hands warm all night.
2.waitRes: "Coward," she whispers, with a smile, and warms them against her cheek instead.

2.title: {name}: The Bath Is Big Enough
2.text: The bathhouse is empty, the steam rising off the water in soft white curls. {name} stands at the edge in a robe, one foot testing the temperature, and glances back over her shoulder. "It's a large bath," she says, as if the thought has only just occurred. "Plenty of room for two. You look like you need it."

image.comp: at the edge of a steaming bath in a loose robe, glancing back at him over her shoulder, inviting
image.setting: private bathhouse at night, steam, paper lanterns

2.goRes: The water is hot and the company is warmer, and neither of them hurries out.
2.waitRes: "Brave, noble Sam," she says, and sinks in with a sigh, tossing him a towel. "Don't look. Or do."

2.title: {name}: Hands and Hesitation
2.text: {name} sits on the edge of the bed with her hands in her lap, twisting the fabric of her sleeve. "I've been thinking about kissing," she says carefully. "And then about what comes after kissing. And then I stopped thinking about anything else." She takes a breath. "May I show you what I've worked out?"

image.comp: sitting on the edge of a bed twisting her sleeve in her lap, looking up with shy brave eyes
image.setting: her bedroom at night, one candle, drawn curtains

2.goRes: It turns out she worked out quite a lot. She apologizes for none of it.
2.waitRes: "Oh. That's nice too," she says, and means it. "A little longer, then, before I show you."

2.title: {name}: A Dare
2.text: {name} slaps a coin down on Sam's desk. "Heads, I pick the next thing we do. Tails, you do." She flips it, catches it, and doesn't look at it. "Heads," she says, with a grin that says it never mattered. "I pick something past kissing."

image.comp: flipping a coin and catching it, grinning, stepping into his space with confident heat
image.setting: his small study at night, lantern on the desk

2.goRes: She never did look at the coin. He suspects it had two heads.
2.waitRes: She laughs and flips again. It lands on the floor. She drags him down to look, and then doesn't let him up for a while, kissing instead.

2.title: {name}: After the Last Guest
2.text: The last guest has gone, and {name} sits on a stool by the dying fire, boots off, rolling her sore shoulders. Sam brings her a cup of tea, and she holds his wrist so the cup trembles. "Everyone takes what they want from me and goes," she says, very quietly. "You always bring tea. Stay a while. I'd like to give something to you."

image.comp: sitting by a dying fire with her boots off, holding his wrist, soft vulnerable smile
image.setting: house parlor after the last guest, embers glowing

2.goRes: She gives, and he receives, and it is the opposite of work.
2.waitRes: They share the pot until it goes cold, her head on his knee. "Next time," she says, drowsy, and means it.

3.title: {name}: Stay Tonight
3.text: {name} is waiting in Sam's room when he comes up, lamp turned low. "I don't want to say goodnight at the door again," she says. "Stay with me tonight."

image.comp: sitting on the edge of a bed in lamplight, holding out a hand to him, soft determined smile
image.setting: his bedroom at night, lamp turned low

3.goRes: The lamp burns down. Neither of them gets up to refill it.
3.waitRes: {name} nods slowly. "Okay. But I'm not going anywhere."

3.title: {name}: The Whole Night
3.text: {name} takes Sam's hand and leads him upstairs without a word. At her door she finally looks back. "I'm sure," she says, before he can ask.

image.comp: leading him by the hand up a narrow staircase, looking back over her shoulder, sure gentle smile
image.setting: narrow lantern-lit staircase at night

3.goRes: The door closes behind them.
3.waitRes: "I said so." She sighs, fond. "Ask me again next week, then. I'll say the same thing."

3.title: {name}: Done Waiting
3.text: {name} kicks Sam's door shut behind her. "I've been patient," she says. "I'm finished being patient."

image.comp: kicking a bedroom door shut, pulling off her outer layer, fierce grin
image.setting: his bedroom at night

3.goRes: Neither of them is patient about it.
3.waitRes: "So is honesty." She grins and leaves. "Honestly, you'll regret that."

3.title: {name}: Gently
3.text: {name} is nervous and won't pretend she isn't. "I want this," she says, holding both his hands. "Just... gently. Okay?"

image.comp: holding both of his hands beside a candlelit bed, nervous brave expression
image.setting: small candlelit bedroom

3.goRes: It is gentle. It's also wonderful, and afterward she won't stop smiling.
3.wait: "We have all the time in the world."
3.waitRes: She lets out a long breath and laughs. "Okay. Okay. Thank you."

3.title: {name}: An Invitation
3.text: A note under Sam's door, in elegant handwriting: "My room. Midnight. Don't be late." When he arrives, {name} is waiting, perfectly composed, except for her eyes.

image.comp: standing by a candlelit window at midnight in an elegant robe, perfectly composed, looking at him with intent
image.setting: elegant bedroom at midnight, candles

3.goRes: Her composure lasts about a minute. It's a very good minute.
3.waitRes: "Then thank you for being punctual." A faint smile. "Another midnight."

3.title: {name}: The One That Counts
3.text: {name} closes her door behind them and leans against it. "Half this town thinks they know what I'm like in bed," she says. "I want one person who doesn't have to guess."

image.comp: leaning back against her closed bedroom door, looking at him, vulnerable and certain
image.setting: her bedroom late at night, a single candle

3.goRes: None of it is new to her, and all of it is. She tells him so, afterward.
3.waitRes: They don't do anything but lie there. {name} says it's the most intimate night she's had in years.

3.title: {name}: Morning After Rain
3.text: The rain hasn't stopped since yesterday, and {name} appears at Sam's door with a blanket around her shoulders and her hair damp. "I don't want to hear it on my own roof tonight," she says. "I want to hear it on yours." She steps inside without waiting for an answer.

image.comp: standing in his doorway wrapped in a blanket with damp hair, soft earnest smile
image.setting: his bedroom at night, rain on the window, lamp burning low

3.goRes: The rain keeps up all night. Neither of them hears it after a while.
3.wait: "It's late. Let me walk you back"
3.waitRes: She laughs, gentle and flustered. "Walk me back, then. Slowly." She takes his arm and it is a very long walk.

3.title: {name}: Ink and Candlelight
3.text: {name} has written Sam a letter. She holds it, folded, against her chest. "I couldn't say it right," she says. "So I wrote it. It's long. It ends with an invitation." She presses the page into his hand. The last line is just three words: "Stay with me."

image.comp: standing at his table, pressing a folded letter into his hand, cheeks flushed, steady gaze
image.setting: his study at night, candlelight, ink pot and quill

3.goRes: He never gets to the second page until morning.
3.waitRes: "Do. Take your time." She touches his sleeve. "I'll be here, reading you."

3.title: {name}: Mine Tonight
3.text: {name} lifts the key to his bedroom from the hook by the stairs, tosses it once, and catches it. "I've decided you're mine tonight," she says. "The house can run itself. Think of it as a day off." She looks as pleased as a cat with cream. Her eyes are not teasing at all.

image.comp: tossing a key and catching it, leaning on his door frame, purring smile
image.setting: upstairs hallway, his bedroom door, lantern light

3.goRes: She locks the door and drops the key down her front. He is clearly not leaving until morning.
3.waitRes: "It really doesn't," she says, and sighs. "Fine. But the key stays with me."

3.title: {name}: Dress Rehearsal
3.text: {name} stands in his doorway in a gown she bought last week and has not yet been seen in. She turns once, slowly, and the silk catches the lamp. "I wanted you to be the first to see it," she says. "And I wanted you to be the one who takes it off." She says it with perfect, courteous composure, and her hands are shaking.

image.comp: turning slowly in an elegant gown in his doorway, poised, steady gaze despite trembling hands
image.setting: his bedroom at night, lamplight on silk

3.goRes: He does, slowly. The gown, it turns out, was very well made.
3.wait: "It's beautiful. Keep it on a while"
3.waitRes: "Then I shall," she says, with a regal nod and the first real smile of the night.

jump.title: {name}: All at Once
jump.text: {name} kisses Sam for the first time in the hallway, and then again, and then she's pulling him toward her door. "I don't want to do this in pieces," she says.

image.comp: pulling him toward her bedroom door by the hand, flushed, kissing him over her shoulder
image.setting: lantern-lit upstairs hallway at night

jump.goRes: One kiss turns into a great deal more than a kiss.
jump.waitRes: {name} stops, catches her breath, and laughs. "...Okay. Slower. Annoyingly."

jump.title: {name}: No Half Measures
jump.text: "I don't do things halfway," {name} says, closing Sam's door behind her. "Never have."

image.comp: leaning back against a closed door, confident heated gaze at him
image.setting: his bedroom at night, one lamp

jump.goRes: She was telling the truth.
jump.waitRes: She laughs. "Fine. A quarter. For now."

jump.title: {name}: Something Shifts
jump.text: Sam is helping {name} carry linens upstairs when she drops them all, takes his face in her hands, and kisses him. When she pulls back, she doesn't let go. "Come with me," she whispers.

image.comp: holding his face in her hands in a hallway, fallen linens around their feet, breathless
image.setting: upstairs hallway, scattered white linens, lantern light

jump.goRes: The linens stay on the floor until morning.
jump.waitRes: "Forget the linens." But she lets him go, laughing. "Next time, forget them faster."

jump.title: {name}: Skipping Ahead
jump.text: "I've never been good at the slow part," {name} admits, already pulling Sam toward her room. "But I'm going to remember this one. Is that all right?"

image.comp: pulling him by the hand toward her room, laughing and a little shy
image.setting: her bedroom doorway at night, lamplight

jump.goRes: She does remember it. So does he.
jump.waitRes: {name} stops in the doorway, considers this, and kisses his cheek instead. "Fine. Slow. Tomorrow."

jump.title: {name}: Storm Night
jump.text: Thunder cracks over the house and every lamp flickers. {name} knocks on Sam's door in her nightgown, clutching a pillow. "I'm not scared," she says, as the next crack shakes the windows. "I just don't want to be alone." She looks at him, then at the bed, then at him again, and steps close enough that the question changes.

image.comp: clutching a pillow in his doorway in a nightgown, lightning behind her, stepping close
image.setting: his bedroom during a thunderstorm, flickering lamp

jump.goRes: The storm passes eventually. Neither of them was paying attention.
jump.waitRes: "The chair," she repeats, deadpan, and laughs. "Very gentlemanly." She takes the pillow back to bed, but keeps the door open a crack.

jump.title: {name}: Wine and Nerve
jump.text: {name} has had exactly one glass of wine, enough to be brave and not enough to be silly. She sets it down, stands, and crosses the room to Sam in four steps. "I'm going to kiss you," she says, "and then I'm going to ask for more. Tell me now if that is a mistake."

image.comp: crossing a room toward him with a determined stride, empty wine glass left behind, bright eyes
image.setting: private sitting room at night, wine bottle on the table

jump.goRes: It was the opposite of a mistake, and she says so several times between kisses.
jump.waitRes: She blinks, then smiles, and sits right back down. "Reasonable. I'll sleep on it. Don't let me lose my nerve."

jump.title: {name}: Long Time Coming
jump.text: {name} has rehearsed this in her head for weeks, and she gets it all wrong anyway. She starts the speech, forgets the middle, and abandons it entirely. "I'm terrible at this," she says, laughing and a little teary. "Can I skip to the part where I don't talk anymore?"

image.comp: laughing and flustered in his doorway, fingers on his sleeve, eyes bright
image.setting: hallway outside his room at night, lantern light

jump.goRes: She does, and it is nothing like her rehearsal, and far better.
jump.waitRes: She takes a breath, tries again, and still forgets the middle, and he loves every second of it.

pent_1.title: {name} Can't Stand It
pent_1.text: {name} has been restless for days and she's done hiding it. She catches Sam in the stairwell, pins him to the wall with both hands, and kisses him before he can say a word.

image.comp: pinning him against a stairwell wall with both hands, flushed, restless heated eyes
image.setting: narrow lantern-lit stairwell

pent_1.goRes: When she finally lets him go, they're both out of breath.
pent_1.waitRes: She groans and thumps her forehead against his shoulder. "Sorry. It's been a week."

pent_1.title: {name} Is Out of Patience
pent_1.text: {name} has been pacing the corridor outside Sam's door for what feels like an hour, and when he opens it she doesn't speak, only grips his lapels and kisses him, hard and a little desperate. "I'm sorry," she says into his mouth. "I'm not sorry. I've thought about this too much."

image.comp: gripping his lapels in a doorway, kissing him hard, flushed restless eyes
image.setting: his doorway at night, corridor lantern

pent_1.goRes: She apologizes again, between kisses, and means it even less.
pent_1.waitRes: She presses her face into his shoulder and breathes. "Okay. Okay. Just give me a minute. A long one."

pent_1.title: {name}: The Last Straw
pent_1.text: It's the way {name} watches him sort the linens that does it, her gaze lingering on his hands. She puts the basket down, shuts the laundry room door, and leans on it. "I've held out as long as I can," she says. "Please don't make me do it from across the room."

image.comp: leaning on a closed laundry room door, breathing a little fast, intense gaze
image.setting: laundry room, hanging sheets, afternoon light

pent_1.goRes: She meets him halfway, and the sheets sway above them.
pent_1.waitRes: She exhales a sharp, frustrated laugh. "Fine. Not here. Somewhere with a lock, then. Soon."

pent_2.title: {name} Has Waited Long Enough
pent_2.text: Kissing isn't cutting it anymore, and {name} says so, at length, while pulling Sam into the nearest empty room.

image.comp: pulling him into an empty room by his hoodie, impatient flushed grin
image.setting: small empty guest room, afternoon light

pent_2.goRes: She's very clear about what she wants. Sam is happy to oblige.
pent_2.waitRes: She lets go with a frustrated sigh. "Fine. But I'm not waiting forever."

pent_2.title: {name}: No More Kisses
pent_2.text: "Kissing isn't enough," {name} says, holding Sam's wrists against the stair rail, pupils wide. "It was never going to be enough. Do you know how many nights I've spent counting the steps to your door?" Her voice is rough, and her whole body hums.

image.comp: pinning his wrists lightly against a stair rail, intense flushed gaze, breathing fast
image.setting: back staircase of the house, evening light

pent_2.goRes: She takes the lead, and all the counted steps are finally worth it.
pent_2.waitRes: She makes an agonized sound and rests her forehead on his chest. "I'm trying. Hold me while I try."

pent_2.title: {name}: Past Caring
pent_2.text: {name} has been on edge since breakfast, and by the afternoon she has stopped pretending otherwise. She walks into Sam's office, turns the key, and leans back against the desk. "I'm not going to be subtle," she says. "I want you. Now. Please."

image.comp: leaning back against his desk with the door locked behind her, wanting gaze, flushed
image.setting: his office in the afternoon, sunlight through the curtains

pent_2.goRes: The ledgers are going to need reshuffling.
pent_2.waitRes: "After the shift," she repeats, agonized, and kisses him once, savagely, to hold him to it.

pent_3.title: {name} Has Had Enough
pent_3.text: {name} shows up at Sam's door at midnight, restless and done pretending otherwise. "I've been lying awake for a week," she says. "Let me in."

image.comp: standing in a doorway at midnight in a loose nightgown, restless heated eyes, one hand on the frame
image.setting: dark hallway at midnight, candlelight

pent_3.waitRes: She exhales hard. "Tomorrow. I'm holding you to it."

pent_3.title: {name}: Not Another Night
pent_3.text: {name} stands at Sam's bedside in the dark, one hand on the blanket. "I can't sleep. I can't think. I can't do anything but want you." Her voice cracks, unashamed. "Please. I'd rather say it plainly than pretend I don't."

image.comp: standing at the side of his bed in the dark, hand on the blanket, raw and unashamed
image.setting: his bedroom in the small hours, a single candle

pent_3.goRes: She slides in beside him, and the long week ends right there.
pent_3.waitRes: She tells him, haltingly and then fluently, and it is the most honest conversation they have ever had.

pent_3.title: {name}: Undone
pent_3.text: {name} meets Sam on the landing, flushed and bare-footed, and takes his face in her hands. "I've tried everything," she says. "Cold water. Long walks. Counting. I'm out of tricks, Sam. I'm just out." She leans her forehead on his.

image.comp: cupping his face on a landing, bare-footed, forehead against his, breathless
image.setting: upstairs landing at night, a single lantern

pent_3.goRes: She follows him in, and the tricks are forgotten.
pent_3.waitRes: "I won't sleep," she says, and sighs. "But I'll lie there and be good. For tonight."

pent_jump.title: {name} Can't Wait
pent_jump.text: {name} has been climbing the walls for days. Tonight she corners Sam, kisses him for the very first time, and doesn't stop at kissing.

image.comp: cornering him against a wall, kissing him hungrily, flushed restless expression
image.setting: dim corridor late at night

pent_jump.goRes: First kiss, and then everything else, in about that order.
pent_jump.waitRes: She stops, breathing hard. "...Sorry. I've been going crazy." She doesn't look very sorry.

pent_jump.title: {name}: Everything at Once
pent_jump.text: {name} bursts into Sam's room without knocking, shuts the door, and says, "I've been trying to work out how to start. I can't. So I'll start with this." She kisses him, then keeps going, in the order that seems right to her, which is every order at once.

image.comp: bursting through his door, kissing him with both hands in his hoodie, wild and flushed
image.setting: his bedroom at dusk, lantern light

pent_jump.goRes: It happens, in an order only she understands.
pent_jump.waitRes: She gasps, steadies, and laughs. "Okay. Breathing. Don't go anywhere."

pent_jump.title: {name}: Past Waiting
pent_jump.text: "I'm not going to wait for a good moment," {name} says, catching Sam in the hall and pushing him against the wall with no ceremony. "There isn't one. There's only this one." Her eyes are fierce and her hands are very sure.

image.comp: pushing him against a hallway wall, fierce eyes, hands sure on his chest
image.setting: house hallway in the evening, lantern light

pent_jump.waitRes: "Slower," she says, and tries, and fails, and kisses him until it's only a very fast sort of slow.

1.title: After Hours
1.text: Mira locks the front door, turns the lamps down one by one, and pours two glasses of the good red she usually saves for regulars who tip well. She slides one across the bar and rests her chin in her palm. "I kept this place running for a man who never once asked how I was," she says, the lantern light soft on the silver in her hair. "You ask every day. It's a problem, Sam. I've grown far too fond of you." She doesn't look away, and she doesn't blush either, which is somehow worse.

image.comp: leaning across the bar counter toward him after closing, two glasses of wine between them, soft fond smile
image.setting: empty lantern-lit lounge after hours, chairs on tables

1.goRes: It is warm and unhurried, tasting faintly of wine, and she leans into it like a woman who has been patient for a long time and sees no reason to apologize for it. When she draws back, her thumb stays on his jaw a moment longer than it needs to.
1.waitRes: Mira laughs, low and fond, and taps the rim of his glass with her nail. "Rush me? Sweetheart, I'm not the one blushing." She ruffles his hair on her way to the stairs and leaves the second glass for him to finish.

2.title: Put the Ledger Down
2.text: It is well past midnight and Sam is still hunched over the ledgers, the candle guttering, the same column added three times. Mira comes in without knocking, plucks the quill from his ink-stained fingers and sets it down like a confiscated toy. "You work too hard. Let someone take care of you for once." She perches on the edge of the desk, smelling of lavender and woodsmoke, and draws him closer by the front of his hoodie until the ledgers are somewhere behind him.

image.comp: sitting on the edge of a cluttered desk, ledger pushed aside, pulling him closer by his hoodie, warm smile
image.setting: small office at midnight, candlelight, stacks of ledgers

2.goRes: She cups his face the way she must have cupped a hundred bruised, tired faces in this house, and for once all that tenderness is aimed at him. He realizes how long it has been since anyone looked after him, and that she knew it before he did.
2.waitRes: "They will tomorrow," Mira sighs, and kisses his forehead like a mother sending a boy to bed. She leaves the candle burning for him anyway, and the sound of her slippers fades down the hall.

3.title: The Lamp in Her Window
3.text: Mira's door stands open and her lamp is lit when Sam comes up the stairs, the warm gold spilling out across the floorboards she knows by sound. She is waiting in her robe, her hair down for once, softer and longer than he ever imagined beneath her pins. "I've decided, Sam," she says, steady as she is with every difficult client. "I'd like you to stay tonight. All night, and breakfast after, if you can stand my cooking."

image.comp: standing beside a lamplit bed in a dressing robe, hair down, holding out her hand to him
image.setting: warm private bedroom above the lounge, lamplight

3.goRes: She takes his hand, draws him over the threshold, and shuts the door on the creaking, humming, thousand-voiced house she has carried on her back for years. For one night, nobody needs her but him, and she lets herself be needed back.
3.waitRes: "I'm sure. Are you?" Mira watches him hesitate and only smiles, unbothered. "Then take a week, love. Take two. The lamp will still be on."

1.title: Nine-Seventeen
1.text: For twelve years, tea at Castle Rosenhal has been served at nine-fifteen exactly, through a mad count, a bankrupt heir and an indifferent duchess. Tonight the tray arrives at nine-seventeen. Cecile sets it down in the moonlit corridor, her spine straight, a single strand of hair loose from her pins. "I was deciding something," she says, and kisses Sam with the same precision she brings to everything: once, certain, a little cool from the draft. Then she checks her pocket watch.

image.comp: standing very close to him in a castle corridor, a tea tray set aside, pocket watch in hand, faint blush
image.setting: moonlit stone corridor of an old castle

1.goRes: "That," says Cecile, slightly out of breath, her fingers still pinching the front of his hoodie, "was not on the schedule." She does not seem to mind in the least, and the watch stays in her pocket.
1.waitRes: "Perfectly." She straightens her apron with two brisk tugs, color climbing the tips of her ears. "Forgive the lapse. It will not happen again." It will, and from the way she avoids his eyes, she knows it.

2.title: The Linen Room
2.text: Cecile asks Sam to help her inspect the linens, which in twelve years she has never needed help with. The linen room is narrow and smells of starch and lavender, shelves of folded white rising on both sides, a single candle on the sill. She turns the key behind them and it clicks very loudly. "This is not on the schedule," she says, unpinning her cap and setting it on a stack of pillowcases. "I am aware." Her hands are perfectly steady. Her pulse, visible at her throat, is not.

image.comp: unpinning her maid cap in a narrow linen room, back against shelves of folded sheets, looking at him through her lashes
image.setting: narrow castle linen room, folded sheets, one candle

2.goRes: She is quiet and careful and precise, as she is about everything, and then at some point she is not careful at all. Afterward the sheets on the nearest shelf are no longer perfectly squared, and she looks at them, and decides to leave them.
2.waitRes: "They do." She pins her cap back on in the dark window glass, perfectly composed except for her ears, which are scarlet. "Another time, then. I will make a note." She does not specify of what.

3.title: Turndown Service
3.text: Cecile has turned down Sam's bed every night at ten for as long as he has owned the castle. Tonight she folds the corner of the blanket, smooths it flat, plumps the pillow, and does not leave. The fire pops. The heavy curtains hold the dark out. "I have run this castle for three owners," she says, hands folded at her waist. "I have never once been off duty under its roof. I would like, for once, to try."

image.comp: standing beside a turned-down four-poster bed, untying her apron, composed but blushing
image.setting: grand castle bedroom, firelight, heavy curtains

3.goRes: She unties the apron slowly, folds it in thirds, and lays it over the chair with the same ceremony she gives the silver. It is the last neat thing that happens all night, and the first time in twelve years that Cecile does not rise before the household.
3.waitRes: "I know." She smiles, very slightly, and the firelight finds the warmth under all that starch. "That is what makes it a choice. Good night, Sam." She turns the lamp down on her way out, as she always does.

1.title: House Rules
1.text: After closing, with the guests gone and the last paper lantern burning low, Tsubaki hauls Sam out to the rock spring behind the bathhouse, steam curling off the black water into the cold. She is already in up to her shoulders, wet hair plastered to her cheek, her late aunt's wooden bucket bobbing beside her. "House rule: last one in pays a forfeit." She flicks water at his shins. "The forfeit is a kiss. I made the rules, so no arguing."

image.comp: sitting at the edge of an outdoor hot spring at night, leaning toward him with a teasing grin, wet hair
image.setting: outdoor rock hot spring at night, steam, paper lanterns

1.goRes: Tsubaki collects with interest, her wet hands warm on his collar, her laugh vibrating against his mouth. Then she splashes him square in the chest and swims off toward the far rocks, singing badly and very happily.
1.waitRes: "Interest accrues daily!" she calls after him over her shoulder, ducking under the steam, delighted by the prospect of an outstanding debt.

3.title: Late Soak
3.text: The springs closed hours ago, and the whole bathhouse hums with the quiet of cooling stone. Tsubaki is waiting in the steam anyway, leaning on her folded arms at the lip of the pool, two little cups of warm sake lined up on the rock beside her. The moon sits in the water like a coin. "Closed means mine," she says. "And tonight, yours. Get in before I change my mind." She is not going to change her mind.

image.comp: lounging in a steaming outdoor spring holding two cups of sake, beckoning him in, playful heated smile
image.setting: secluded rock hot spring at night, steam, moonlight, lanterns

3.goRes: The sake goes cold on the rock. Tsubaki sings one verse, gives up on it halfway, and for once the off-key voice that fills the bathhouse every night goes quiet and soft near his ear.
3.waitRes: Tsubaki laughs so hard she slips under and comes up sputtering, hair in her eyes. "The boilers! Fine, boss. Go check your boilers. Next time I'm not asking."

1.title: Three Hundred Years
1.text: Vesper drifts through Sam's wall a little past midnight, trailing a hem of old silk that makes no sound, and hovers at the foot of his bed with the moon showing faintly through her shoulder. The air goes cold and smells of dust and long-dead roses. "I've decided to find out whether I can still be kissed," she announces, lifting her chin like a lady of her own era. "It's been three hundred years. Hold very still." Her hands, when they reach for his face, are shaking.

image.comp: translucent and faintly glowing, floating close to him, cupping his face in her hands
image.setting: dark manor bedroom, moonlight, dust motes in the air

1.goRes: It is cold for one heartbeat, then it isn't. Vesper pulls back, wide-eyed, one hand pressed to where her heart would be. "Oh," she says, barely audible. "Oh, I remember now." The candle on his nightstand flares up on its own.
1.waitRes: "You're the only one who doesn't scream." She sighs, impossibly dramatic, and sinks by slow degrees into the floorboards until only her indignant eyes remain. "I shall haunt you about it. Gently."

3.title: Solid
3.text: The full moon pours through the old manor's curtains, and Vesper is more solid tonight than Sam has ever seen her: warm hands, color in her cheeks, the folds of her gown stirring against the floor. She presses his palm flat to her ribs. "A heartbeat," she whispers, astonished. "I swear I can feel it." Her eyes shine. "I don't know how long this lasts. Let's not waste a minute of it."

image.comp: glowing softly in moonlight, solid and warm, pulling him toward a canopy bed by both hands
image.setting: old manor bedroom under a full moon, curtains stirring

3.goRes: They don't waste one. She laughs at the sensation of everything, of warmth and weight and breath, and he holds on as if she might slip through his arms, which by dawn she does, fading back to mist with a smile.
3.waitRes: "I'm dead, Sam. Safe is relative." She sighs, the edges of her already blurring a little in the moonlight. "There will be other moons. I have, after all, a great deal of time."

3.title: A Wager
3.text: The tavern is empty after closing, chairs up, the last lamp swinging, and two enormous tankards slam down on the bar hard enough to jump the coins. "Drinking contest," Hilde says, cracking her knuckles. "Loser does whatever the winner says." Sam loses so badly that it becomes local legend. Hilde, barely flushed, one boot up on the rung of his stool, smells of malt and woodsmoke and victory. "Upstairs, boss. That's what I say."

image.comp: slamming an empty tankard on the bar, flushed and grinning triumphantly at him
image.setting: empty tavern bar after closing, tankards everywhere

3.goRes: Hilde doesn't believe in doing anything halfway, and she has very clear ideas about what she won. Her grip on his hand is calloused and certain, and she doesn't let go all the way up the stairs.
3.waitRes: She laughs so hard she nearly slides off her stool, thumping the bar. "Fine! Rematch next week. Train up, boss. I'll keep the barrel cold."

1.title: After the Encore
1.text: After the last show, with the audience gone and one candle burning in the footlights, Sylphine takes Sam by both wrists and pulls him up onto the empty stage. Dust motes drift in the warm light. "You're always watching from the back," she says. "Come learn a step." He is terrible. She doesn't let go of his hands, and the step, whatever it was, ends a great deal closer than it began, her forehead nearly touching his.

image.comp: dancing with him on an empty stage, foreheads almost touching, hands joined
image.setting: candlelit stage after the show, empty seats in shadow

1.goRes: Sylphine laughs against his mouth, the sound light and bright as a bell in the hushed theater. "Terrible footwork," she murmurs. "Excellent finish." Somewhere in the dark seats, the only applause is the pounding of his own heart.
1.waitRes: "Coward," she says fondly, and spins away into the wings in one long, perfect line, her shoes whispering over the boards. She is smiling when the curtain swallows her.

2.title: Rehearsal
2.text: Sylphine books the stage for a private rehearsal and meets Sam barefoot in a loose white practice dress, the curtains drawn, a single candle by the footlights. "I'm choreographing something new," she says, with the earnest focus she gives every piece. "It needs a partner." She presses a page of notes into his hand. The margins are full of her careful elven script. Most of the notes are not about dancing, and she studies the rafters while he finds that out.

image.comp: barefoot on an empty stage in a loose rehearsal dress, holding out a page of notes to him with a sly smile
image.setting: dim rehearsal stage, a single candle, curtains drawn

2.goRes: Sylphine is extremely thorough about blocking. The rehearsal runs very late, and she corrects his posture, his breathing and his hands with the same patient murmur, until nothing is left to correct.
2.wait: "I don't think I can dance that."
2.waitRes: "Nobody can, yet." She tucks the page into his pocket and pats it flat, eyes bright. "Practice. I'll hold the stage for you."

3.title: The Finale
3.text: "Every piece needs a finale," Sylphine says, standing in Sam's doorway with moonlight in her loose hair and her dancing shoes dangling from one hand. After a century of rehearsed perfection, her voice has a small unguarded tremble in it. "I've been writing ours for weeks. I only ever wanted one performance. I don't mind if no one claps."

image.comp: standing in a bedroom doorway with her hair loose and her dancing shoes in one hand, soft determined smile
image.setting: his bedroom at night, moonlight through the window

3.goRes: It is the best thing she has ever choreographed, and she says so, several times, between breaths. For once she is not counting beats at all.
3.waitRes: "Then we'll keep rehearsing." She kisses his cheek, light as a held note, and pads off down the hall with her shoes swinging, humming the missing bars.

1.title: Adorable
1.text: Zaria perches on the edge of Sam's desk in the plush red lamplight, one ankle crossed over the other, tail curling lazily behind her like a question mark. "You blush every time I walk past," she says, amused. "It's adorable. Humans are adorable." She leans down until her horns almost graze the lamp and her voice drops to a purr. "Let's see what you do if I do this."

image.comp: perched on the edge of a desk, leaning down toward him with an amused predatory smile
image.setting: plush velvet office, red lamplight

1.goRes: What he does is turn very red, from collar to hairline, which Zaria considers a complete success. Her tail flicks with satisfaction and she takes her sweet time pulling away.
1.waitRes: "You don't." She lets him go anyway, laughing, and trails a clawed fingertip along his jaw as he slips free. "Run, little human. I'll catch you later."

3.title: Owner's Privilege
3.text: The Veil's finest suite is all silk drapes and slow red candlelight, the hum of the floor muffled behind the door. Zaria closes it with her back and leans there, tail swaying, looking Sam over like a ledger she has finally decided to settle. "I've run this floor for longer than you've been alive," she says. "I've never once taken a night for myself. Tonight I'm giving myself the night off. And I'm spending it on you."

image.comp: leaning back against a closed door in a lavish room, looking him over with a slow confident smile
image.setting: the Veil's finest suite, silk drapes, red candlelight

3.goRes: She does, in fact, know exactly what she's doing, every bit of it, and she lets him see that she is enjoying it too. For a woman who keeps a ledger of everyone's favors, she asks for nothing in return.
3.waitRes: "Everyone owes me something." She opens the door with a theatrical sigh, tail flicking. "I'll add it to your tab. With interest, little human."

1.title: Boots
1.text: The inn is quiet, the last coach long gone, and a single lantern burns over the front desk. "I can tell where a man's been by his boots," Bettina says, not looking up from her ledger, pen scratching on. "Yours have been pacing in front of my desk for a week." She caps the ink bottle, finally lifts her warm brown eyes, and crooks one finger. "Well? Come here."

image.comp: leaning across the reception counter toward him, ledger pushed aside, knowing warm smile
image.setting: inn entrance hall at night, lantern-lit wooden counter

1.goRes: She kisses him across the counter like she's been planning the angle for days, one hand flat in the middle of his chest. She has. When she lets him go, the ledger is somehow upside down.
1.waitRes: "Mm-hm." Bettina goes back to her ledger, smiling at the page, and the pen resumes. "Bookings are open whenever you are, dear. I never close the books on a good customer."

2.title: Stocktake
2.text: Bettina asks Sam to help count linens in the stockroom, a job that takes about three minutes and which she has already finished. The room is cramped, lantern-lit, smelling of cedar and clean cotton. She shuts the door with her hip and leans on the crates with her clipboard held to her chest like a shield she isn't using. "Business is good," she says. "So I'm taking a bonus." Her cheeks are pink, but her eyes are not shy at all.

image.comp: leaning against stacked crates in a stockroom, holding a clipboard, crooking a finger at him
image.setting: cramped inn stockroom, shelves of linens, one lantern

2.goRes: Bettina is very particular about getting full value, and she checks her work as carefully as any column of sums. By the end the clipboard has slid onto the floor, and neither of them bends to pick it up.
2.waitRes: "Cheapskate." She swats him with the clipboard, grinning, and cheerfully opens the door. "Quarterly, then. I'll mark my calendar."

3.title: Checked In
3.text: The inn is dark except for the lamp at reception, and Bettina is waiting behind the counter with a brass room key pinched between two fingers. She slides it across the worn wood to him with one slow push. "Room six," she says. "I've already checked us in. The sheets are fresh. I did them myself." One eyebrow rises. "Don't make me refund it."

image.comp: sliding a brass room key across a counter toward him, eyebrow raised, playful smile
image.setting: inn reception desk late at night, a single lamp

3.goRes: Room six has the best bed in the Wayfarer, and Bettina picked it personally. For a woman who counts everything, she loses count of the hours, and she doesn't ask him to pay for any of them.
3.waitRes: "No refunds," she says, but she tucks the key into his pocket anyway and pats it twice, her smile gone warm. "It'll keep, dear. I'm good at keeping things."

1.title: Patching Up
1.text: Kaede comes back from sparring with split knuckles and a scowl, and sits at the kitchen table with the first-aid kit open and her hand held out like it belongs to someone else. While Sam winds the bandage around her palm, her fox tail curls up and around his arm all on its own. Halfway through, she grabs his collar and kisses him, quick and clumsy and fierce. "Don't make it weird," she says, ears flat against her head.

image.comp: leaning in to kiss him while he bandages her hand, fox tail curled around his arm, ears flattened shyly
image.setting: kitchen at night, a first-aid kit open on the table

1.goRes: He doesn't make it weird. He kisses her back, slowly, careful of her hand, and her tail goes completely puffy while her ears slowly rise from flat to a very pleased upright.
1.waitRes: "Forget it. Heat of battle." She yanks her hand free, half-wrapped bandage trailing, and is out the door before he can finish, tail lashing and the tip of every ear red.

3.title: No More Waiting
3.text: Kaede climbs in through Sam's window at midnight with her boots in one hand, silent as a Copper Fox on a night raid, moonlight silvering the red of her tail. She drops to the floor, brushes off her knees, and meets his eyes without a trace of her usual swagger. "Adventurer rule," she says. "If you want something, you clear the dungeon before someone else does. I'm done being the scout who hangs back."

image.comp: climbing in through a moonlit window, kicking off her boots, determined grin, ears perked
image.setting: his bedroom at midnight, window open, moonlight

3.goRes: She brings the same focus to this as to any boss fight, and the same fierceness, but there is a gentleness under it that she hides in her tail, wrapped tight around his wrist. Someone left her in the dark once. Tonight she is the one who stays.
3.waitRes: "Doors are for people who knock." She climbs back out over the sill with a grin, tail swishing, and pauses with one leg over. "Next time I'm not leaving."

1.title: Overtime
1.text: The accounts office is silent but for the hiss of the lamp, papers fanned across every desk, and Yui stands holding a ledger against her chest like a shield. She hasn't let go of it in ten minutes. "Back home, every time you covered my shift, I wanted to say something," she says, voice small and very even. "I never did. That was the first life." The stapler she arrived with sits on the desk between them, absurd and dear.

image.comp: standing close to him in a small office at night, holding a ledger to her chest, nervously looking up at him
image.setting: lamplit office, papers everywhere, late night

1.goRes: The ledger hits the floor. Neither of them picks it up for a while. When she exhales it shakes, and she laughs through it, six years of filed-away feelings finally coming off the shelf.
1.waitRes: "I know." She smiles shakily and retrieves her ledger, hugging it again. "Maybe in a few more weeks I'll be brave enough to do it anyway. I'm working on it, Sam. I'm keeping notes."

2.title: Second Life Rules
2.text: Yui has written a list, in her tidy accountant's hand, titled SECOND LIFE RULES. She sits on the edge of the bed in the candlelight, shoulders stiff, and hands the page to Sam without looking at him. Rule one is "Say what you want." She stares fixedly at the wall while he reads rule two, her cheeks burning so hot the candle seems pale beside them.

image.comp: sitting on the edge of a bed, staring at the wall with burning cheeks while he reads a handwritten list
image.setting: small bedroom at night, a single candle

2.goRes: It turns out to be a very good rule, and she discovers rules three through five by herself. She laughs in the middle of it, breathless, because she has finally said what she wants out loud.
2.waitRes: "Right. Yes. Good." She takes the list back with both hands and adds a tiny footnote in pencil. "Pending." Her ears are red, but she is smiling at the paper.

3.title: No Last Train
3.text: "In Tokyo I always had to catch the last train," Yui says at Sam's door, one hand on the frame, the lamplight warm behind him. She says it carefully, like a sentence she's rehearsed in the mirror. "Every single night, I left. I took the train home alone." She takes a breath, and her voice cracks, gentle and brave. "There's no last train here."

image.comp: standing in a bedroom doorway at night, holding the door frame, shy brave smile
image.setting: his bedroom at night, warm lamplight

3.goRes: She stays. The lamp burns low, and in the morning she is still there, her glasses crooked on the nightstand and a soft, astonished smile on her face, which is the whole point.
3.waitRes: "Yeah." She laughs a little, wipes her eyes with her sleeve, and squeezes his hand. "I'm getting good at not running for the train."

3.title: Contract Terms
3.text: Nerys sits on the edge of Sam's desk with her legs crossed and the glowing contract unrolled across her lap, bat wings half-spread, the magic circle on the floor pulsing a faint violet beneath her heels. "Clause forty-one," she reads, in her driest voice. "The bound party is entitled to reasonable sustenance." She lowers the scroll and looks at him over the top, her pupils slits in the candlelight. "I have been extremely, unreasonably patient."

image.comp: sitting on a desk with crossed legs, holding a glowing contract scroll, smirking down at him, bat wings spread
image.setting: his study at night, candlelight, a magic circle glowing on the floor

3.goRes: There is no clause forty-two. Nerys makes one up on the spot, and under all the lawyerly wit her hands are tentative at his shoulders, as if she can't quite believe this one is hers to keep and not on loan.
3.waitRes: Nerys groans and flops backward across the desk, scroll and all, wings splayed over his papers. "Humans. Fine. Read your fine print. But I am billing you for the wait."

1.title: Check-Up
1.text: Elowen insists on checking Sam's heartbeat. The infirmary smells of dried herbs hanging from the rafters, and the afternoon sun is thick as honey. She presses her ear to his chest, closes her eyes, and goes very quiet. "It's fast," she reports, professionally. Then, smaller: "Mine is too." She kisses him so quickly he almost misses it, then hides her face in his shirt, the tips of her ears blazing.

image.comp: leaning her ear against his chest, eyes closed, deeply blushing, healer's satchel on her shoulder
image.setting: small infirmary room with herbs drying from the rafters

1.goRes: He puts his arms around her and doesn't let go, and after a long while she stops hiding and lets herself be held, listening to his heart settle. "Oh," she whispers into his shirt. "That's how it works."
1.waitRes: She makes a tiny strangled noise and flees to the herb garden, satchel bumping at her hip. A moment later her laugh drifts back through the open window, bright and embarrassed and happy.

2.title: Bedside Manner
2.text: Elowen has been reading. She stacks the heavy medical tomes very neatly on Sam's desk, squaring the edges, and a pressed sprig of rosemary falls out of one and she doesn't notice. "Human medical texts," she says, to the candle, "are quite detailed about certain things. I should like to check my understanding." Her pointed ears are crimson, and her hands fidget with the hem of her sleeve. "With a reliable colleague."

image.comp: stacking medical books on a desk, crimson pointed ears, looking at him with nervous determination
image.setting: small study lit by a candle, books and dried herbs

2.goRes: She is a diligent student, asking careful questions in a tiny voice, and she takes notes afterward on a scrap of parchment. Sam finds this deeply familiar, and deeply endearing.
2.waitRes: "Yes. Good. Methodical." She hugs the books to her chest and nods very fast. "One chapter at a time. I've marked the page."

3.title: Starlight
3.text: On the hill outside town, far from the lantern glow, the sky is crowded with the constellations of her homeland. Elowen spreads a blanket over the cool grass and takes Sam's hand in both of hers. Her fingers are trembling, though her voice is clear. "Elves wait a very long time for things," she says quietly, eyes on the stars, then on him. "I'm finished waiting."

image.comp: sitting on a blanket under a sky full of stars, holding his hand, shy hopeful smile
image.setting: grassy hilltop at night, sweeping starry sky, town lights far below

3.goRes: Afterward she names every star above them, one by one, curled against his shoulder, her voice slow and happy. Somewhere past the third constellation she runs out of names and just stays.
3.waitRes: "We won't." She leans her head on his shoulder and points out a star. "Elves are very good at not rushing. Stay a while and look with me."

1.title: Chapter Twelve
1.text: The barracks room is spartan: a narrow cot, a candle, a stack of romance novels she has not bothered to hide tonight. Adelheid reads Sam a chapter aloud in her parade-ground voice, "for literary critique." In chapter twelve the knight kisses her lord. Adelheid stops reading. She closes the book on her finger, crosses the stone floor in three armored strides, and does exactly that, eyes squeezed shut, gauntlet clenched. Then she stands to attention, scarlet to the collar.

image.comp: standing stiffly in armor holding a closed romance novel, cheeks scarlet, kissing him with her eyes squeezed shut
image.setting: spartan barracks room, a candle, a stack of romance novels

1.goRes: "That," she says hoarsely, "was a dramatic reading." She does not let go of his hand, and the steel of her glove warms slowly against his fingers.
1.waitRes: "It was IMPLIED." She salutes, turns smartly, and marches out, armor clanking down the corridor. The book stays behind on the cot, bookmarked at chapter twelve.

2.title: Chapter Twenty
2.text: There is a new bookmark in the novel on Sam's pillow, set at chapter twenty, and a note in Adelheid's stiff, square handwriting: "For critique. I await your report." When he opens the door, she is standing in the candlelit corridor in full armor, at attention, staring at a point somewhere above his head. A flush has climbed all the way to her hairline. She has been standing there, by the look of it, for some time.

image.comp: standing at attention outside a bedroom door in armor, staring straight ahead, deeply blushing
image.setting: candlelit corridor at night

2.goRes: Adelheid takes notes, for accuracy. Her pen shakes only a little, and by the end it has fallen to the floor along with the rest of her careful composure.
2.waitRes: "Of course. A thorough review takes time." She salutes, stiff as a lance, and leaves very fast. Her footsteps break into something close to a run at the end of the hall.

3.title: The Final Chapter
3.text: Adelheid has finished the novel. She sets it on Sam's table, squared with the edge, and begins to unbuckle her gauntlets one at a time. Each buckle clicks in the candlelit hush. "In the books, the knight always waits for her lord to say something," she says, not quite steady. "I have waited longer than any knight in the books. I am done waiting for you to say it."

image.comp: unbuckling her armored gauntlets beside a candlelit bed, steady determined gaze at him
image.setting: his bedroom at night, candlelight, armor pieces on a chair

3.goRes: The armor takes a long time to come off, plate by plate, and neither of them is in any hurry. Beneath it, the Dame who has guarded relics and bishops turns out to be shy, and exceedingly brave.
3.waitRes: "Is my own to give." She buckles the gauntlets back on, one at a time, perfectly unoffended, and bows her head. "When you are ready, my lord."

1.title: Winner's Prize
1.text: The training yard is gold with sunset dust, and Natsuki has just pinned Sam to the ground for the fifth time, wooden sword skidding off across the packed earth, her knee planted by his hip and her breath ragged from laughing. "Winner gets a prize," she announces, and kisses him before he can ask what the prize is. Then she sits back on her heels, looking horrified at her own mouth.

image.comp: pinning him to the floor of a training yard, wooden sword tossed aside, flushed and grinning
image.setting: dusty training yard at sunset

1.goRes: He loses the rematch on purpose, and she knows, because she has been beating him since they were kids three doors apart. She claims the prize anyway, softer this time, her fingers lingering in the dirt of his hair.
1.waitRes: "My yard, my rules!" She scrambles up, red to the ears, snatches her sword and is gone across the dusty ground before he can even sit up.

3.title: Victory Feast
3.text: Natsuki comes back from a dungeon job still buzzing with adrenaline, armor dented, a bag of gold slung over one shoulder, the smell of rain and iron on her. She drops the bag at Sam's feet in the lamplight and the coins chime. Her bravado slips for one second, and under it is a girl who spent three years alone in a world that never called her "Natsu." "I spent three years alone here," she says. "I'm done being careful."

image.comp: standing in a doorway in dented armor, dropping a bag of gold, flushed and fierce, sword still on her hip
image.setting: his room at night, lamplight

3.goRes: The armor ends up all over the floor. So does the gold. When she says his name afterward, she says it as if he were a place she'd finally found a way back to.
3.wait: "Let me get you some food first."
3.waitRes: "FOOD. Okay. Good point." She eats like a horse, then falls asleep on his shoulder mid-sentence, sword and all. "Tomorrow," she mumbles. "I'm holding you to it."

1.title: Last Call
1.text: The bar is dim after last call, chairs up on the tables, the smell of spilled whiskey and orange peel in the air. Kanako pats Sam's cheek the way she always does. "Look at you, all grown up." Her hand stays. She looks at it, there against his face, like it belongs to someone else, and the loudest laugh in the room has gone quiet. "Oh," she says. "Oh, I see." And she kisses him.

image.comp: leaning on the bar after closing, cupping his cheek, surprised soft expression
image.setting: dim bar after last call, chairs on tables

1.goRes: For once in her life, Kanako doesn't have a single thing to say. Her hand is still on his cheek, her eyes wide and a little bewildered, and the silence of the empty bar is the sweetest sound.
1.waitRes: "I have." She laughs, a little shaky, and the laugh is not nearly as loud as usual. "Ask me again sober, Sammy." She means it. She polishes the same glass three times.

3.title: Not the Boy Next Door
3.text: "I've called you Sammy for six years," Kanako says, closing his door behind her and leaning on it. Her hair is down, the pins left somewhere, and the lamp makes her look softer, younger. "Tonight I'm going to call you something else." For once she's the one blushing. All the confidence she wears behind the bar, the hostess's, the bouncer's, has slipped away.

image.comp: leaning against a closed bedroom door, blushing, warm teasing smile, hair let down
image.setting: his bedroom at night, a single lamp

3.goRes: She shows him instead of telling him. Kanako has always been better at showing, and her laugh, when it finally comes, is low and private and not for anyone else's ears.
3.waitRes: "Coward." She ruffles his hair, fond, a little relieved, and sets her hand on the doorknob. "I'll ask again. You know I will."

1.title: Like in the Dramas
1.text: Akari drags Sam out into the rain beneath a single umbrella, rain drumming on the canvas and the lanterns smeared gold on the cobbles. "In every drama, the first kiss is in the rain," she says, shining. "I've been practicing this scene for years." She rises on tiptoe, eyes closed, and kisses him. Then she pulls back, considers, and makes him do a second take, for the lighting.

image.comp: under a shared umbrella in the rain, standing on tiptoe to kiss him, eyes shining
image.setting: lantern-lit cobbled street in the rain at night

1.goRes: The second take is better. So is the third. The umbrella blows away down the street and neither of them notices, soaked and laughing, her cold fingers curled in his hoodie.
1.waitRes: "That's the point!" She laughs, wipes the water from her eyes, and drags him home anyway, hand tight in his. "Rain check. Literally."

2.title: Episode Two
2.text: "In dramas, episode two is where it gets serious," Akari says, sitting cross-legged on Sam's bed in her pajamas, hair in a messy bun, a bag of snacks she has clearly brought for the occasion. "I've seen a lot of episode twos. I just never got to play one." She pats the blanket beside her, grinning, but her knee is bouncing, and under the bravado there is the girl who used to walk him to the station.

image.comp: sitting cross-legged on a bed in pajamas, patting the blanket beside her, mischievous excited grin
image.setting: his bedroom at night, lamplight

2.goRes: Akari was underselling how many episode twos she has seen, and she laughs through every scene, delighted and a little overwhelmed. The snacks end up forgotten on the floor.
2.waitRes: "Ugh, those are the WORST." She pouts, flops backward, and steals his pillow in protest. "Fine. But I'm not leaving. I'll just sulk here."

3.title: Season Finale
3.text: Akari has made a sign. It says SEASON FINALE in enormous marker letters, a little crooked, and she is holding it in front of Sam's door like a shield, her hair loose and her ears pink. For the first time all season she isn't performing. "No more cliffhangers," she says, and her voice drops. "I'm not Kenta's sister tonight. I'm a grown woman, and I know exactly what I want."

image.comp: holding up a handmade sign in a doorway, nervous brave grin, hair down
image.setting: his bedroom doorway at night

3.goRes: It's a very good finale. Akari gives it ten out of ten, and then, still holding his hand, quietly adds that she'd like it renewed.
3.waitRes: She groans and slides down the door frame to the floor, the sign dropping into her lap. "Fine. Season two. But the sign stays up."

1.title: Terms
1.text: Marisol slaps a contract on Sam's desk hard enough to make the inkwell jump. The office smells of lamp oil and old paper, and she is perched on the corner of the desk like a cat on a ledger. "Proposal: one kiss. Nonbinding." He starts to read the fine print. She takes the page back, eyes bright, and her smile is entirely unfair. "Counteroffer: stop reading," she says, and reaches for his collar to close the deal herself.

image.comp: leaning across a desk over a contract, pulling him in by his collar, smug triumphant smile
image.setting: the owner's office, ledgers and contracts, lamplight

1.goRes: "Pleasure doing business," she murmurs against his mouth, and he can feel her grinning. Her fingers stay curled in his hoodie like she's afraid he'll renegotiate.
1.waitRes: "You don't HAVE a lawyer." She rolls the contract into a tube and bops him on the head with it, laughing, but her ears are red. "Offer stands. It never expires, Sam. I checked."

2.title: Revised Terms
2.text: "I've revised the terms," Marisol says, and the key turns in the office lock with a click that sounds very final. Lamplight catches the gold in her hair and the ledgers behind her are for once completely ignored. "Section two. Considerably expanded." She tosses the contract over her shoulder without looking, and it skids across the floor into the dark. Her voice stays level, but she's biting her lip, and he can tell she's nervous under the swagger.

image.comp: tossing a contract over her shoulder, locked office door behind her, confident challenging smile
image.setting: the owner's office at night

2.goRes: Marisol negotiates every single point, loudly at first and then not at all. Sam loses every clause, and happily signs away the rest.
2.waitRes: "Forty-eight hours," she says, retrieving her contract with great dignity. "Then I'm renegotiating in person, and I don't lose."

3.title: Closing the Deal
3.text: Marisol is sitting on the edge of Sam's bed with two glasses and a dusty bottle, the label so old the ink has gone brown. It was her father's best, the one he swore he was saving, for what, he never said. Lamplight turns the wine the colour of garnets. She's kicked off her boots and her toes curl against the rug. "He saved it his whole life," she says. "Then he left it behind with the debt. I'm done saving things."

image.comp: sitting on a bed holding two glasses of red wine, a dusty bottle beside her, warm resolute smile
image.setting: his bedroom at night, lamplight

3.goRes: The cork comes out with a soft sigh, and for a moment Marisol looks like someone setting down a very heavy ledger. She laughs, a little wet-eyed, and doesn't look away from him.
3.waitRes: "He's not here to mind." She drinks Sam's glass as well, but gently, and her smile is only a little bruised. "Fine. Next time. The bottle's not going anywhere. Neither am I."

1.title: Noblesse Oblige
1.text: Etiquette lessons are held in the old ballroom, where afternoon light slants through tall windows and dust turns slowly in the gold. Seraphine has been drilling Sam on bows and forms for an hour, ring glinting on her glove. "A lord kisses a lady's hand like so." He does. "Adequate." But she doesn't take her hand back, and her chin has come up in that proud way that means she's terrified. Her cheeks are pink to the ears. "Now. Not the hand."

image.comp: standing in a faded grand hall, holding out her gloved hand to him, chin raised, cheeks pink
image.setting: dusty ballroom of an old castle, tall windows, afternoon light

1.goRes: "...Acceptable," Seraphine manages, a little breathless, her gloved fingers tightening on his sleeve. "We shall have to practice further, for form's sake." They do, and the Rosenhal ancestors in their portraits are scandalised.
1.waitRes: "Coward." She sweeps toward the door in a rustle of skirts, spine perfectly straight, but at the threshold he sees her smile, and the hand he kissed pressed to her heart.

3.title: The Rosenhal Bed
3.text: The great chamber of the castle is cold at the edges and warm only where the fire reaches. Seraphine stands beside the Rosenhal bed, four hundred years of carved oak and faded canopy, one hand resting on a bedpost as if to steady herself. Her hair is down, pale gold over her shoulders, the first time he has seen it so. "Every Rosenhal has been miserable in it," she says, voice wobbling. "I'd like it to have one good memory."

image.comp: standing beside an enormous antique four-poster bed, proud chin, blushing, letting her hair down
image.setting: grand castle bedchamber, faded tapestries, firelight

3.goRes: Seraphine lets out a breath she seems to have held since the family's fortunes fell, and the proud line of her shoulders softens. "Then do not stand there like a footman," she whispers, almost laughing.
3.waitRes: "I'll decide what I deserve." Her voice wobbles, and she tightens her grip on the bedpost until her signet ring catches the fire. "Ask me again when you've stopped being an idiot."

1.title: A Century of Watching
1.text: The pavilion's paper lanterns come on one by one at dusk, floor by floor, a slow tide of amber climbing the walls. Ilyana stands at the balcony rail with Sam, silver hair stirring with its tiny pearls in the evening breeze, the whole city softening below. She has watched this very sight for a hundred years, and he can see in her pale gold gaze that it's never been shared. "I've watched lovers here for a century," she says quietly. "I'd like to stop watching."

image.comp: on a balcony at dusk, turning toward him with a calm ancient gaze, lanterns glowing behind her
image.setting: pavilion balcony at dusk, hundreds of paper lanterns lighting up

1.goRes: A century of practice shows, and also, strangely, a century of waiting. Her hand rises to his cheek as if he were something rare, and Sam forgets the lanterns entirely.
1.waitRes: "So were most of them." She smiles, unhurried, and turns back to the glow. "I can wait. I am very good at it, and you are worth the practice."

2.title: Lessons
2.text: Ilyana closes the shutters of her study one at a time, and the city noise falls away into silk and quiet. Incense curls up from a brass dish; cushions the colour of old wine are heaped by the low table. She doesn't hurry, she never does, but when she glances back over her shoulder her smile is warm and a little bold. "A century teaches you things," she says. "I find I'd like to teach some of them to you."

image.comp: closing ornate shutters in a study, glancing over her shoulder at him with a serene knowing smile
image.setting: elegant elven study, silk cushions, incense

2.goRes: Ilyana is an extremely patient teacher, and an unexpectedly tender one. Her laugh, when he blushes, is soft as the incense.
2.waitRes: "Of course." She opens the shutters again and lets the evening back in, serene and unoffended. "I have waited a hundred years. Another week will not hurt me."

3.title: Lantern Night
3.text: The night of the lantern festival the pavilion garden is full of rising light: hundreds of paper lanterns lifting into the dark, each carrying a wish. Ilyana holds hers at the water's edge, then lets it go and watches it climb. Her hand finds Sam's, cool, then warm, and her pearls shine faintly in the glow. "I have spent a century being the patroness," she says. "Tonight I would like to simply be yours."

image.comp: releasing a paper lantern into the night sky, holding his hand, soft serene smile
image.setting: pavilion garden at night during a lantern festival, lanterns rising

3.goRes: Ilyana's serenity cracks into something shy and luminous, and she leans into him as the last lantern clears the trees. "Then I am," she says, and sounds amazed by it.
3.waitRes: "They are beautiful," she agrees, and lays her head on his shoulder, silver hair spilling over his hoodie. "Next festival, then. I am rather fond of this view with company."

1.title: Something in the Dark
1.text: Midnight patrol of Hollowmere Manor means a lantern, a bag of salt, and Ines's grip on Sam's sleeve hard enough to bruise. The corridor smells of dust and cold candle wax. Then something lunges out of the dark, a white shape with a shriek, and it's Vesper, giggling. Ines grabs Sam so hard they both go down, the lantern rolling away with a faint ghostly glow. She's on top of him, breathing fast, her scar pale against her jaw. Neither of them moves. She kisses him.

image.comp: sprawled on top of him on a dark manor floor, lantern rolling away, startled then determined
image.setting: dark manor corridor at midnight, a fallen lantern, a faint ghostly glow
