jump.text: Lyn has been circling Sam for weeks and hates it. She finally corners him in the hallway by the back stairs. "I don't do slow. I've turned down titles and armies and I'm not going to be defeated by a skinny bookworm in a hoodie." She plants a hand on the wall beside his head. "So. Do I win, or do I have to try harder?" She has smelled of rain and leather all week, and the whole house has noticed, and she knows that, and does not care.

image.comp: pinning a hand against the wall beside him, fierce grin, a faint blush across her nose
image.setting: narrow back-stairs hallway of the house, lantern light

jump.goRes: She kisses him the way she does everything, all at once and at a full run, and he is gently surprised to find he is keeping up.
jump.waitRes: "A minute." She narrows her eyes, then lets him go with a snort. "I've waited on armies for longer. I'll be on the roof."

1.title: Evening Vespers
1.text: Rhea has turned the little storeroom off the east hall into a chapel of sorts, with candles and a single brass bell. Sam finds her there after closing. "I was tending a great many souls once," she says, serene as a held breath. "Tonight I find I would rather tend one." Her hand rests against his cheek, cool and impossibly gentle. The smell of wax and old incense hangs about her, and the small bell throws a tiny shadow on the wall.

image.comp: standing among candles in a small chapel nook, one hand raised to his cheek, a serene and tender smile
image.setting: tiny candlelit chapel in a storeroom, brass bell, folded vestments

1.goRes: Her lips are cool, then not. She lets out a breath like someone setting down a very old weight.
1.waitRes: "Of course." She smiles, unoffended and unhurried. "I have waited centuries, child. I can wait for your heart to catch up."

2.title: Confession
2.text: She asks Sam to sit with her in the garden alcove, where the lanterns are dim. "People used to kneel to confess," Rhea says, smoothing her robes. "No one has asked for my confession in a very long time." Her fingers find his, and she holds them with startling warmth. "I want to be touched without being worshipped. Can you do that?" Night jasmine drifts in from the beds, and when she speaks again her voice is nearly human, nearly frightened.

image.comp: seated on a garden bench, holding his hand in both of hers, an uncertain, honest expression
image.setting: moonlit garden alcove with hanging lanterns and night-blooming flowers

2.goRes: He's very careful with her. She is very quiet, and then not so quiet, and her sigh is that of someone who had forgotten she was allowed.
2.waitRes: "Slowly." She laughs, low and pleased. "Yes. You understand mercy better than most priests. We shall go slowly."

3.title: A Night Without Vigil
3.text: Rhea is waiting in her room with the bell silenced and the candles lit low. The matron's composure is there, but her hands are not quite steady. "I have kept vigil for the faithful for six hundred years," she says. "Tonight I wish to be only a woman who is wanted. Will you stay?" The room smells faintly of lavender. Her hair is unbound, and it spills nearly to her waist, silver in the candlelight.

image.comp: sitting at the edge of a large bed in a loose robe, hands folded, a nervous but dignified smile
image.setting: elegant bedroom with soft candlelight and heavy curtains

3.goRes: He stays. The candles burn low and nobody watches the door, and she does not seem like anything but a woman who is wanted.
3.waitRes: "I am older than most mountains, Sam, and I am sure." A tender smile. "But you may take the night to be certain. I shall be here."

jump.title: Quiet Hour
jump.text: Rhea finds Sam alone in the kitchen at some deep hour of the night, stirring warm milk. Without a word she takes the spoon and sets it aside. "I have been very good for a very long time," she murmurs. "I find I am tired of it." She steps closer, and for a moment the air around her feels ancient and warm at once. The clock in the hall has ticked past three. The steam rises, and for once she does not seem eternal, only tired and warm.

image.comp: stepping close in a dim kitchen, spoon set aside, gaze steady and warm with a hint of mischief
image.setting: dim kitchen at night, a pot of milk steaming on the hearth

jump.goRes: Time seems to forget itself. Rhea kisses him like someone remembering a song they once knew by heart.
jump.waitRes: "So you are." She laughs, soft and amused, and pours herself a cup. "Then we'll sit. I will find my courage over the dregs."

1.title: Encore
1.text: Manuela is still in her stage dress when Sam finds her at the back of the empty hall, humming the last bars of an aria to the dusty chairs. "Nobody claps when no one is looking," she says, with a wry little laugh. "Be a darling and applaud." He does. She bows, takes his hand, and stays bowed a beat too long. Dust turns slowly in the single beam of the lantern, and she is smiling the brittle way people do when they are afraid to hope.

image.comp: taking a theatrical bow in a stage dress, one hand holding his, a playful and slightly vulnerable smile
image.setting: empty stage and hall after the show, a single lantern left lit

1.goRes: She hums against his mouth, a startled note that she lets fade, then kisses him again. "Mm. Bravo, darling."
1.waitRes: "Always the gentleman." She flutters her fan, winks, and sweeps away. "I'll keep the front row warm."

2.title: Husband Hunting
2.text: Manuela has been through four lemon wines and a long list of her disappointments. "I have been looking for a husband for years," she says, resting her chin on her hand. "Every one wants a diva or a doctor. None of them want to know whether I take my tea sweet." She fixes Sam with a long look. "You asked. Do you realize how rare that is?" Her lipstick has smudged on the rim of the glass. The ghost of a tune hums under every word, as it always does with her.

image.comp: slumped charmingly against the bar, chin on her hand, sad smile turning warm
image.setting: back corner of the bar, empty glasses, low lamp

2.goRes: She sets her hand over his, and her flirtatious patter falls away. What follows is slower and gentler than either of them expected.
2.waitRes: "I know, dear." A rueful chuckle. "Hope is stubborn, though. Pour me another, and we'll pretend I'm not hopeful."

3.title: The Doctor Is In
3.text: Manuela turns up at Sam's door with a medical satchel and a very straight face. "Professional concern. You've been working far too hard. I'm prescribing rest, wine, and a good deal of company." The satchel lands on the chair. Her hand lands on his chest. "I'll be monitoring your pulse personally." The satchel smells of herbs and tincture, the way a real physician's does, and her fingers on his wrist are surprisingly steady.

image.comp: leaning in the doorway with a doctor's bag over one shoulder, hand on his chest, teasing smile
image.setting: Sam's bedroom lit by a single lamp, a bottle and two glasses on the table

3.goRes: His pulse is, she reports with great satisfaction, scandalous. The treatment lasts until well after the wine.
3.waitRes: "Doctors hear that every day, and it is always a lie." She pats his cheek. "Rest tonight, then. The treatment will keep."

jump.title: Opera Fever
jump.text: Manuela sings through the entire evening, a full aria for the lounge crowd, her voice rolling over the room like warm honey. When the last note ends she skips the applause, marches straight to Sam, and kisses him in front of everyone. A beat later she goes pink to the ears. "Oh dear. That was meant for the dressing room." Silence follows, then a scatter of boots and delighted whistles, and the diva who has faced a thousand audiences cannot lift her head.

image.comp: caught mid-kiss then pulling back, hand to her cheeks, flustered and delighted
image.setting: lounge stage with lanterns and astonished patrons behind

jump.goRes: The room gives them a long, delighted cheer. Manuela hides her face in his shoulder, laughing, and does not let go.
jump.waitRes: "Yes, yes. Dressing room. I'm so sorry, darling." She fans herself furiously, and her eyes sparkle all the same.

1.title: Night Watch
1.text: Lethe has the door shift, which means she is awake and hostile to everything. Sam brings her a bowl of soup anyway. She sniffs it, glares at him, and eats it. "Humans," she mutters, tail twitching. "You give things and want nothing. It makes me suspicious." A pause. "...I do not hate it." Past midnight the hall is quiet, the lamp throwing her long shadow across the door, ears swiveling toward every creak.

image.comp: sitting on a stool by the door with a bowl in her hands, ears angled toward him, guarded but softening
image.setting: front entrance hall at night, lantern on the wall, shut door

1.goRes: She sets the bowl down and, without comment, kisses him. It's brief and fierce, like a claw's swipe, and she wipes her mouth afterward as if to check it was real.
1.waitRes: "I am." She narrows her eyes, then looks away. "You are the only one who did not ask for anything. Remember that."

2.title: Grooming
2.text: Lethe stands in the washroom with her tail soaked after a rainy patrol, scowling at a comb she cannot reach. Sam offers to help, and she nearly bites him for it. Then, stiffly, she turns and presents her back. "Slowly. If you tug, I will know." Her purr starts on the second stroke. She pretends it's a cough. The room smells of damp fur and lavender soap. Her tail trembles at the tip whenever the comb catches a tangle.

image.comp: back turned and tail held out, glancing over her shoulder with an embarrassed glare, ears flat then softening
image.setting: small washroom with warm steam and a single window, a comb on the sill

2.goRes: The purr grows. She turns around, pulls him in by the front of his hoodie, and remarks quietly that she has decided to allow more.
2.waitRes: "I will." Her tail curls around his wrist. "Not yet. Do not look so proud."

3.title: Claiming the Night
3.text: Lethe shows up at Sam's room off-shift, arms crossed, tail lashing. "I have thought it over. I distrust you less each week. It is irritating." She steps in and shuts the door with her heel. "A warrior should take what she has decided on. I have decided on you." Moonlight cuts across the floorboards. She stands there as if facing down a charge, but her ears keep drifting flat and then upright again.

image.comp: stepping inside and kicking a door shut, arms crossed but a small shy smile tugging her mouth
image.setting: Sam's room with the window open to a clear cold night

3.goRes: She is as forceful as she is blunt, and then startlingly soft. When dawn comes she is still there, curled against him and deeply offended at how comfortable it is.
3.waitRes: "I have thought. You are the one who must think." She snorts, but a touch lingers on his sleeve. "Do not take long."

jump.title: Claw Marks
jump.text: Sam leans in to pull a loose thread from her cloak, and Lethe goes rigid, tail bristling. A heartbeat of pure hissing stillness. Then she grabs his collar and kisses him, hard, as if daring him to flinch. "Do not mention this," she warns. "Do not tell the others. Do not make it a story." The wall is cold behind him, her breath warm against his jaw, and her heart is hammering fast enough to feel through her cloak.

image.comp: gripping his collar, ears pinned, fierce and flustered glare after a kiss
image.setting: the hallway by the front door, shadows from a hanging lantern

jump.goRes: He keeps his word. She keeps pressing closer, and her tail slowly stops lashing.
jump.waitRes: "No." Ears flat. Then, muffled, "...Later. Perhaps." She's gone before he can see her face.

1.title: Moonlit Path
1.text: Panne walks the garden path alone every night and never explains why. Tonight Sam falls into step beside her without asking, and she lets him. "Most humans fill silence," she says at last, tall against the moonlight, long ears tilted toward him. "You do not. I find I have stopped counting the exits when you are near." Crickets stop and start in the hedges. Her stride is silent on the gravel, but tonight it is a shade slower than it should be.

image.comp: walking a moonlit garden path, long ears tilted toward him, a rare soft look
image.setting: garden path with lanterns and silver moonlight on the hedges

1.goRes: She lets him. After a long moment she turns, tucks her hair behind her ear, and kisses him as lightly as a rabbit crossing snow.
1.waitRes: "I will." The ghost of a smile. "Do not mistake slow for no. I wait. It is what my people know best."

2.title: Trust
2.text: Panne is seated stiffly on the library window seat with her knees drawn up when Sam finds her. "My people were hunted for what we are," she says, eyes on the glass. "I was taught not to be touched by strangers. You have not been a stranger for some time." She holds out one hand, palm up, trembling just slightly. The glass fogs where she breathes, and her knuckles are pale around her knees. She has not looked away from him once.

image.comp: seated in a window seat with knees up, one palm extended toward him, braced and hopeful
image.setting: quiet library nook with rain on the windowpane

2.goRes: He holds it, then more. She lets him closer by degrees, and every inch is a gift she hands over deliberately.
2.waitRes: "I know." She exhales shakily and keeps his hand. "That is why I could ask. Give me a moment."

3.title: Burrow
3.text: The room is dark when Panne lets Sam in, and it has been rearranged into something like a burrow, blankets heaped in the corner, a lantern turned low. "I do not do this lightly," she says, one ear flicking. "I have never brought anyone into my den. Not even in my head." She sits and pats the heap beside her. The blankets smell of cedar and warm wool. Her ears droop low, a small tell she would never admit, and her fingers pluck at the hem.

image.comp: sitting on a nest of blankets, patting the space beside her, long ears low and shy, tall frame folded small
image.setting: her private room with blankets heaped like a nest and a low lantern

3.goRes: He settles in beside her. She tucks herself under his arm, quiet and impossibly warm, and the night belongs to them.
3.waitRes: "It is a lot to give," she says gravely. "Think on it. I will keep the blankets."

jump.title: Spring Hare
jump.text: A hard spring night and Panne is sleepless, restlessly pacing the kitchen, ears twitching. Sam arrives for water and she suddenly closes the gap, pressing her forehead to his and then his mouth. "Forgive me," she whispers. "I have run so long. I am tired of running from this one thing." The window is open to the damp air, and the lamp is out. Her long ears tremble as she backs a step away, and then forward again.

image.comp: pressed close to him with her forehead against his, eyes closed, ears trembling
image.setting: dim kitchen with a window open to a warm spring night

jump.goRes: She lets out a startled laugh into the kiss, as if she had spooked herself, then stays right where she is.
jump.waitRes: "I am. I think." She retreats a pace, breathing hard. "Give me time to be brave twice."

1.title: Sky Watcher
1.text: Corrin sits on the sill of the attic window most nights, looking at the town as if it were a map she is still learning. Sam joins her with a blanket. "Everything here is so loud and so kind," she says, dreamy. "In the fortress I never saw so many strangers smile." She leans her head on his shoulder and then, shyly, up. She tucks her hands inside the blanket, and the faintest glow of heat shimmers off her where the lantern light touches.

image.comp: sitting on a window sill with a blanket around her shoulders, leaning against him, soft dreamy smile
image.setting: attic window above the rooftops with a view of town lights

1.goRes: Her lips are warm, almost fevered, and she makes a small astonished sound, like she's tasted a new fruit.
1.waitRes: "Oh. Yes." A shy, sleepy smile. "There is no hurry. I have only just seen the sky."

2.title: Dragon Warm
2.text: Corrin's hands run hot whenever she's flustered, a trait of that old blood. Tonight she stands in Sam's doorway holding a mug of cocoa that is nearly boiling. "I am sorry. I was going to be calm about this." Her pupils flicker faintly. "May I hold your hand? I think it would help us both." The cocoa steams in her fingers, nearly boiling. A faint scale-pattern shimmers on her wrist where she's nervous.

image.comp: standing in a doorway holding a steaming mug, eyes with a faint draconic glint, hopeful and nervous
image.setting: Sam's room, soft lamplight, a rug and shelf of books

2.goRes: Her palm is hot as a hearth stone, and he finds he does not mind at all. She leans in, bold with sweetness, and learns what else warmth can mean.
2.waitRes: "Of course." She curls up beside him on the rug and laughs at herself. "I will cool down. A little."

3.title: Two Homes
3.text: Corrin sits cross-legged on Sam's bed with a letter she has not finished in a month. "I always belonged to two places and neither was really mine," she says. "I think this might be the first home I chose." She sets the letter aside. "I would like to choose you too, if you will let me." Outside, the last carts of the day rumble home. Her gaze goes between the letter, the window, and him, and settles at last on him.

image.comp: sitting cross-legged on a bed holding an unfinished letter, glancing up with open sincerity
image.setting: Sam's bedroom with a quilt, lamplight, a night window

3.goRes: She chooses him slowly, gently, and with a trembling sort of bravery. The letter stays unwritten, and it no longer matters.
3.waitRes: "I think so." She hugs the letter to her chest. "But I will finish this first. Wait for me."

jump.title: Cold Hands
jump.text: Corrin finds Sam on the porch in the winter chill and presses his cold hands between her feverish palms. "You are freezing." Her fingers warm his through and through, and she looks up at him through the steam of her breath. "I hope this is not strange. I feel like I have been waiting for an excuse." Frost gathers along the rail, and the steam of her breath curls up between them. A faint flush of gold creeps along her cheeks.

image.comp: holding his hands between hers with breath visible in cold air, shy and affectionate
image.setting: front porch in winter night with frost on the railings and warm lantern glow

jump.goRes: She is so warm that the cold forgets him entirely. Her laugh hiccups out in a puff of breath.
jump.waitRes: "Yes. Yes, of course." She squeezes once more. "Inside, then. But I am not letting go of your hands."

1.title: Posture
1.text: Eirika still stands as though a crown rested on her head, even sweeping the lounge floor after closing. Sam teases her gently about it. "Habit," she apologizes, which makes him laugh. "I am sorry, I did not mean...!" She stops. She laughs too, helplessly. "I think I have not laughed like this since the war ended." Her broom stands forgotten against the wall. She has not slouched once in the whole conversation, even now, even laughing.

image.comp: laughing helplessly with a broom in hand, composure slipping, hand over her mouth
image.setting: lounge after closing, chairs stacked, lanterns burning low

1.goRes: She kisses him with the grave sincerity she brings to everything, and apologizes afterward, and then kisses him again.
1.waitRes: "Of course. Forgive me." She flushes. "I tend to treat every feeling like a duty. Let me learn to let this be pleasant."

2.title: A Princess Off Duty
2.text: Eirika asks Sam to walk with her through the evening market, not as a princess, but as nobody in particular. She buys a paper lantern, loses it to the wind, and chases it laughing. At the canal edge she turns, hair loose, cheeks bright. "Is this what it is like? To simply be a person?" The paper lantern bobs away on the wind, and she is breathless, hair sticking to her cheek, as joyful as a girl of fifteen.

image.comp: standing at a canal edge with hair loose, laughing, flushed with delight
image.setting: evening market by a canal with paper lanterns and warm lights

2.goRes: She takes his arm, and later, in the quiet of the stair, she takes more. She is earnest even about this, every touch an honest question.
2.waitRes: "Yes. Of course." She slips her arm through his anyway. "Just as far as the stair, then. I would like to keep the lantern light a little longer."

3.title: The Crown Set Down
3.text: Eirika waits on the edge of Sam's bed, in a plain nightgown, with her hands pressed together. "I have led armies and buried friends," she says quietly. "I have never been asked what I wanted. I want this. I want you. And I am terrified." A tremulous smile. "Please be patient with me." The candle gutters, and she catches the flame with her palm as if it were a thing to defend. Her voice wobbles on 'terrified'.

image.comp: seated on the edge of a bed in a simple nightgown, hands clasped, brave and anxious
image.setting: Sam's room by candlelight, a plain coverlet and an open window

3.goRes: He is. She learns, tentatively, that a princess may be held without needing to hold up a kingdom.
3.waitRes: "You are kind to offer." She nods, steadying. "Another few days, then. I will practice courage."

jump.title: Apologies
jump.text: Eirika bumps into Sam in the corridor with an armful of linens and apologizes seven times. He catches the sheets, then her elbow. "Sorry, I... Oh." She stops, staring at where his hand rests on her arm. "I have apologized for everything for years. I do not want to apologize for this." And she kisses him, linens and all. The corridor smells of clean cotton. A single sconce throws her shadow long, and her heart is plainly pounding in her throat.

image.comp: kissing him with an armful of linens, eyes shut, a determined blush
image.setting: upstairs corridor with stacked linens and a dim sconce

jump.goRes: The linens fall, forgotten. She does not apologize once.
jump.waitRes: "Oh! I am so sorry!" Red to the ears, she gathers the sheets and stops. "...No. I am not sorry. Only early."

1.title: Lesson Plan
1.text: Byleth is grading the house staff's reading exercises, which no one asked for, at the kitchen table. Sam sits down across from her. "You made a mistake on line four," she says flatly. "I did not correct it. I wanted you to stay." Her face does not change at all. The tip of her ear turns bright pink. Her quill scratches in the quiet. She has been rereading the same page for ten minutes, and the candle has burned down a finger's width.

image.comp: sitting at a table with a quill and papers, expression unreadable, ear faintly pink
image.setting: kitchen table with papers, a candle, and a half-finished tea

1.goRes: Her eyes widen by a hair. Then she pulls him down by the sleeve and returns the favor with unnerving precision.
1.waitRes: "Understood." She turns the page. Her pen hovers a beat too long. "I will adjust the schedule."

2.title: Massage Hours
2.text: Byleth works the knots out of Sam's shoulders in the dim storeroom after a double shift, hands strong and exact. "You hold tension here," she says. "And here." A pause. "I enjoy this more than I expected." Her thumbs slow. In the half-light, the corner of her mouth gives the smallest, rarest curve. The air smells of warm oil and cedar. Her hands have stilled on his shoulders, and she is watching the back of his neck with great attention.

image.comp: standing behind him, working his shoulders, a very faint smile at the corner of her mouth
image.setting: small storeroom turned massage room with warm oil lamp

2.goRes: She studies his face, nods once, as if concluding an experiment, and explores a great deal more.
2.waitRes: "Alright." Utterly neutral, and yet she lays the blanket over his shoulders before she goes.

3.title: Hypothesis
3.text: Byleth knocks at midnight and enters before he answers. "I have formed a hypothesis," she says, straight-backed. "I believe I want to stay in your bed. I would like to test it." She says it with the same expression she'd use for a lesson plan. She is holding the doorknob very tightly. She has rehearsed this; he can tell, because she arrives at each word on time, like soldiers. Her knuckles are white on the knob.

image.comp: standing very straight in a doorway, gripping the doorknob, deadpan with a flicker of nerves
image.setting: Sam's room at midnight, a single candle

3.goRes: The result, she reports afterward, in a tiny voice, is conclusive. She does not leave in the morning.
3.waitRes: "Acceptable." She nods once. "I will refine the experiment. Do not tire of me."

jump.title: Silent Type
jump.text: There's a battle exercise on the training lawn and Byleth lands Sam flat on his back in the grass with a gentle, precise sweep. She kneels over him, braced on one hand, breathing a little heavier than the throw deserved. "...I have lost track of the lesson," she admits, expressionless. The grass smells of sun and cut hay. Her braid has come loose in the tumble, and she does not seem to notice at all.

image.comp: kneeling over him in the grass, one hand braced beside his head, deadpan but visibly flustered
image.setting: training lawn behind the house in afternoon sun

jump.goRes: She blinks. A moment later she is kissing him in the grass with an awkward, devoted care, as if learning a new form.
jump.waitRes: "Dismissed." She stands and offers a hand, expression perfectly flat, ears glowing. "Tomorrow. Same time."

1.title: Morning Prayer
1.text: Celica prays before every shift, kneeling at the little window in the staff hall. This morning Sam kneels beside her without a word, and she opens one eye, smiling. "You are not much for hymns, are you?" she whispers. "It's all right. I think you pray with your hands, the way you carry things for everyone." She touches his sleeve. A candle stub burns on the sill, and she has tucked her hair behind one ear, as she does when she has made up her mind.

image.comp: kneeling by a sunlit window with folded hands, one eye open and smiling at him
image.setting: staff hall window with morning light and a small shrine candle

1.goRes: Her lips are soft and quietly joyful, like a blessing returned. She laughs under her breath. "I think the saints are blushing."
1.waitRes: "Of course." She bows her head and peeks at him through her lashes. "I shall add you to my list. At the top."

2.title: The Missing Friend
2.text: Celica sits on the back steps in the dusk, turning an old charm over in her fingers. "I came all this way to find someone I lost," she says. "I have not found him. But I found a place where I'm useful, and a person who listens." She leans her head on Sam's shoulder. "Is it selfish to want to be happy while he is still missing?" The herb bed smells of thyme and rosemary. Her charm catches the last light, small and worn from being held so often.

image.comp: seated on stone steps holding a small charm, leaning her head on his shoulder, hopeful and a little sad
image.setting: back steps of the house at twilight, herbs growing by the wall

2.goRes: He tells her no, it's not selfish, and she believes him enough to turn her face up. Her touch is earnest and warm and a little shaky.
2.waitRes: "Yes." She presses the charm to her heart. "I will wait. But thank you for the shoulder."

3.title: Blessing
3.text: Celica comes to Sam's room in her white sleeping gown, clutching her hands as if praying through every step. "I asked for guidance," she says, breathless. "And all I could think was: 'Be brave. Be kind. Be his.'" She laughs at herself, eyes shining. "I do hope that was not blasphemy." A gentle rain taps the glass. Her hands tremble a little on her gown, though her smile is steady, and she keeps it up like a lamp.

image.comp: standing in a white sleeping gown with hands clasped at her chest, flushed, hopeful smile
image.setting: Sam's bedroom with a single candle and a rain-streaked window

3.goRes: He tells her it wasn't. The night is gentle, devout, and often interrupted by helpless giggles.
3.waitRes: "I am nearly sure." She nods, resolute. "Nearly is enough for prayer. Let me be sure for you."

jump.title: Brave Steps
jump.text: Celica trips on the cellar stairs carrying wine, and Sam catches her. They stand frozen, her hand fisted in his hoodie. "Oh. Thank you. I..." She lifts her eyes. "I have been so careful to be good. Just once, I would like to be impulsive." And she kisses him on the stairs. The cellar smells of oak and cool stone. A bottle rolls to a stop at their feet, and neither of them reaches for it.

image.comp: caught mid-stumble in his arms, hand clutching his hoodie, kissing him with flushed surprise
image.setting: narrow cellar staircase with wine racks and dim lantern light

jump.goRes: She breaks away giggling and breathless. "Heavens. That felt like a miracle."
jump.waitRes: "Right. Yes!" Mortified and radiant, she scrambles upright. "I will do better. I will take the next stair... and the next step too, later."

1.title: Tea Etiquette
1.text: Jinhsi serves tea in the ceremony room with a calm that could still a harbor. Sam fumbles his cup and she steadies it with a touch. "A magistrate learns to hold a thousand burdens without a ripple," she says quietly. "But I find myself wishing someone would take one from me." Her dragon-gold eyes rest on him, gentle and questioning. Steam rises from the pot in a thin ribbon. Her sleeves are folded with perfect symmetry, and the faint gold of her horns catches the lamp.

image.comp: pouring tea with graceful precision, gold eyes lifted to him, composed smile with the faintest tremor
image.setting: tea room with paper screens, a low table and soft lantern glow

1.goRes: She turns her palm into his. When she kisses him, it is like a long-held breath, serene and gracious.
1.waitRes: "Very well." She pours a second cup, her composure perfect. "I have waited decades for this city to be at peace. A few weeks are nothing."

2.title: Letter Home
2.text: Jinhsi is at her writing desk composing the dispatch she should have sent a month ago. "I keep finding reasons to postpone my return," she admits. "The reasons all have your face." She lays down the brush. "A magistrate should not be so easily moved. I should like to see what happens if I allow it." Ink dries on the half-finished letter. The brush has left a faint line on her fingertip, and she has not noticed, or has chosen not to.

image.comp: seated at a writing desk with a brush set down, turning her face to him, calm but flushed
image.setting: study with ink stones, rolled letters and an evening lantern

2.goRes: She is gracious even in surrender, and astonishingly warm. It is the first time in a century that she has set the city aside.
2.waitRes: "Wisdom." A small, wry smile. "I have a great deal of it. Let me spend a little foolishness, later."

3.title: Without the Robes
3.text: Jinhsi has let her hair down, and the robes of office hang on a screen. Without them she seems smaller, shy of her own bare shoulders. "Many have served me," she says. "No one has seen me as I am when no one is watching. I would like it to be you." Her voice is steady. Her hands are not. Outside, a watchman calls the hour. Her hair spills past her hips, uncoiled, and she looks both younger and far older than anyone has seen her.

image.comp: standing beside a folding screen with her formal robe hung behind her, hair loose, brave and vulnerable
image.setting: private chamber with silk hangings and moonlight through paper screens

3.goRes: He is careful, as one is with a priceless thing that is also very much alive. Her laughter, when it comes, is low and astonished.
3.waitRes: "Thank you." She bows, a perfect small bow. "The city can spare me another night. But not many."

jump.title: Dragon Impulse
jump.text: A festival drum thunders in the street and Jinhsi steps out onto the balcony, face flushed with the rhythm. Sam finds her there, hands gripping the rail. "Forgive me," she says, low. "It is the blood. Tonight I do not feel composed." She turns and kisses him, quick and sure, and her eyes shine gold in the dark. Firelight and paper lanterns throw gold across the wood. Her horns glint, and the careful mask of office has slipped entirely away.

image.comp: gripping a balcony rail with the glow of festival lanterns behind her, turned to him, golden eyes bright
image.setting: balcony above a festival street with drums, lanterns and fireworks

jump.goRes: She leans into him, and her composure falls like a dropped veil. The drums keep going, long after they stop hearing them.
jump.waitRes: "Yes. No." She laughs, stilled, regal again. "I will return to my senses. Do not judge the magistrate for the festival."

1.title: Investment Review
1.text: Carlotta sits at the corner table with the ledger and an expression of tidy disdain. "Your margins are acceptable. Your staffing is sentimental. Your owner, however..." She snaps the book shut, tapping it against her palm. "...is proving a better investment than projected." She rises, small and exact, and kisses him once as a gesture of closing the deal. The brandy glows amber in the lamplight, and her heeled boots rest on the rung of the chair, one ankle crossed with practiced ease.

image.comp: tapping a closed ledger against her palm, a sharp amused smile, her pistol holstered at her hip
image.setting: corner table in the lounge with a ledger and brandy

1.goRes: The kiss is brief and brisk, then not brisk at all. Carlotta pulls back, flushed, and straightens her cuffs. "Provisional, of course."
1.waitRes: "Hm." She tilts her head, eyes narrowing in approval. "Hard to buy. Interesting. I will raise my offer."

2.title: Collector
2.text: Carlotta shows Sam her private gallery, a room of sculptures and curios she's brought across the sea. "Every piece I own, I chose carefully." She stops before a small bronze fox. "Few people understand what I'm really looking for. Not a thing. A person who does not mind being looked at." Her eyes linger on him. "You do not flinch." The room smells of lacquer and sea salt. Her gaze moves over each piece as a jeweler's would, then back to him, unhurried.

image.comp: standing beside a shelf of curios with a small bronze figure in her hand, appraising him with a flushed smile
image.setting: private room of curios and art, a spotlight of lamplight

2.goRes: She looks at him as she looks at art, with patience, then with wanting, and then she touches him as though he were not for sale but for keeps.
2.waitRes: "Of course not." A rare, softer smile. "Some pieces are never sold. I'll wait for you to decide you are one of them."

3.title: The Pistol on the Nightstand
3.text: Carlotta sets the ornate pistol on Sam's nightstand like a signature. "A formality. I am armed, you are not, and I would like us both to be at ease." She sits on the bed, her heels hooked together, a proud lift to her chin. "I have never trusted anyone enough to take it off. Tonight I intend to." Her ring catches the candle as she folds her hands. She has not removed her gloves, and the stiffness of her shoulders gives her away.

image.comp: sitting on the edge of a bed with an ornate pistol laid on the nightstand, proud posture with a nervous flush
image.setting: Sam's bedroom with a candle and a polished dresser

3.go: Take the gun off the table
3.goRes: He moves it to the dresser. She notices, and lets out a slow, startled exhale. Whatever contract this is, there are no clauses left.
3.waitRes: "I know I don't." Chin up. "That is why it matters. Ask me again next week; the offer stands."

jump.title: Hostile Takeover
jump.text: Carlotta corners Sam behind the bar after a long argument about prices, her face flushed from wine and winning. "You infuriate me," she says, jabbing a finger into his chest. "You are stubborn, you are sentimental, and I cannot stop looking at your mouth." Before he answers she grabs his lapel. "Consider this a merger." The bar glass between them is still half full, and her cheeks are flushed with wine and the unholy pleasure of a good argument.

image.comp: grabbing his hoodie with a flushed triumphant smile, finger pressed to his chest
image.setting: behind the bar, glasses and bottles glinting

jump.goRes: It's a very good merger. Carlotta emerges with her hair out of place and the unforgivable expression of someone who has won something.
jump.waitRes: "Terms!" She laughs, thrilled. "Excellent. I adore negotiation. I'll draft something. Foreplay, perhaps."

1.title: Moon Dance
1.text: Hsin dances alone on the rooftop terrace when the moon is full, her white tail trailing like mist. When Sam arrives she does not stop. "Do you know what I guard?" she says, in rhythm with her steps. "What cannot be held. Come closer and tell me if you are the kind to try." The dance ends with her hand against his chest. Moonlight pools on the tiles. Her white tail trails behind her in the air like smoke, and where she steps, no sound follows.

image.comp: mid-dance on a terrace with her white tail sweeping behind her, one hand reaching toward him, moonlit mystery
image.setting: rooftop terrace under a full moon with silver light

1.goRes: She smiles slowly. Her kiss tastes of night and cold water, and she vanishes into her dance again before he can ask what it meant.
1.waitRes: "A riddle: what is delayed and not denied?" She tilts her head, tail swaying. "Think on it. I'll wait among the stars."

2.title: Riddle
2.text: Hsin sits cross-legged on the tea room mat, tail curled around her knees. "Answer one question and I'll answer yours," she says. "What is closest when it is farthest, and farthest when it is closest?" Sam guesses. Wrong. She leans forward, eyes glimmering. "Try again, and I'll let you pay the forfeit." Her tea has gone cold, forgotten. The corner of her mouth quirks every time he guesses wrong, and she is plainly enjoying herself.

image.comp: leaning across a low table with a glimmer in her eyes, tail curled, playful and enigmatic
image.setting: tea room with a low table and a single moonlit window

2.goRes: The forfeit is long, slow and delightful. She never does reveal the answer, but afterward she sighs like someone who has heard one.
2.waitRes: "Do. The riddle will keep. So will I." Tail flicking, she vanishes into the corridor, leaving a single petal on the cushion.

3.title: Mortal Shape
3.text: Hsin sits at the edge of Sam's bed, hands folded, white ears twitching. "I have worn this shape for centuries," she says, "but never felt it. Never until you looked at me." She laughs, low and strange. "Teach a guardian spirit what a body is for, Sam. I would like to learn from someone gentle." A single petal drifts in at the window. Her eyes shine silver in the dark, and for the first time her voice does not sound rehearsed.

image.comp: sitting at the edge of a bed with folded hands, ears twitching, curious and soft-eyed
image.setting: Sam's bedroom with moonlight across the quilt

3.goRes: He teaches her with patience and delight. By morning she is dazzled, and so quiet he is almost worried, until she says: "Again, tomorrow."
3.waitRes: "Spirits do not lie... often." A smile. "Wait if you must. The moon will return."

jump.title: Fox Fire
jump.text: Hsin catches Sam at the foot of the stairs, her eyes glowing pale in the dark, tail curled around his arm. "A spirit should not want this," she says, as if reciting. "A guardian should not want this." She leans up and kisses him, and her voice is nearly human: "I want this." Her breath fogs in the cold stairwell. A faint, pale glow follows her fingertips, and it flickers whenever she pauses.

image.comp: kissing him at the foot of a staircase with pale glowing eyes, tail wrapped around his arm
image.setting: dark stairwell with a single lantern and white petals drifting

jump.goRes: The glow in her eyes steadies to a warm moon-silver. She pulls away just enough to whisper that mortals have a clever custom.
jump.waitRes: "Mm." She withdraws, tail dragging reluctantly. "A riddle for you: when is a spirit most mortal? When she must wait."

1.title: Quiet Between Songs
1.text: Cartethyia hums on the back terrace, a thin clear tune for the harbor boats. When Sam sits beside her she lets the song fade. "The city never stops talking," she says softly. "You talk less than most. I find I rest around you." Her slender hand finds his. "It has been four hundred years since I rested in anyone's company." A gull cries somewhere over the harbor. Her voice drops lower, as though afraid to disturb the water, and her wings press close to her back.

image.comp: seated on a terrace railing with hands clasped around his, eyes closed in a soft hum, small and serene
image.setting: back terrace overlooking the harbor lights at night

1.goRes: She sighs, like a tide going out, and kisses him back with unhurried grace. Somewhere beyond the rooftops, the sea lies still.
1.waitRes: "Thank you." She hums a few notes. "Tides wait for no one, but they always return."

2.title: Rapier Lesson
2.text: Cartethyia shows Sam how she holds her slender rapier, standing behind him with her arms around his, guiding his grip. "Lightly. As if holding a bird." Her breath stirs his hair. The lesson stops being about swords, and she doesn't move away. "I think you are a very patient bird," she murmurs. The training hall smells of beeswax and old oak. Her breathing is slow, and a strand of pale hair has fallen across his shoulder.

image.comp: standing close behind him guiding his hand on a rapier hilt, soft and curious smile
image.setting: training hall with polished wood floors and slanting evening light

2.goRes: They are very close. She seems to hold her breath, then lets it go all at once, and learns how well a quiet voice can speak when it is allowed to.
2.waitRes: "Of course." She slides the rapier back into its sheath, her cheeks pink. "The bird thanks you. The bird would like to continue the lesson, eventually."

3.title: High Tide
3.text: Cartethyia opens her door at the end of the hall in a long pale gown, her small wings folded close. "Sam. I have sung the sea calm for centuries. Tonight, I find I cannot calm myself." She tries to smile. "If you stayed, I think the waters would settle." The hallway is quiet but for the distant sea sound of the town. Her fingers fidget with the hem of her sleeve, an unfamiliar human habit.

image.comp: standing in the doorway of a softly lit room in a long pale gown, wings folded, tremulously hopeful
image.setting: her tidy room with pale curtains and a shell on the windowsill

3.goRes: He stays. The storm in her goes down like the sea at dawn, slow, enormous, silver.
3.waitRes: "I am as sure as I am afraid." A tender smile. "Come back another night. I will leave the window open."

jump.title: Overwhelmed
jump.text: The city is too loud tonight, and Cartethyia flees to the linen closet where it is quiet. Sam finds her sitting between the shelves, knees to her chest. "I only needed to be still," she whispers. "But with you, stillness feels... less lonely." She leans into him, trembling, and then kisses him with unexpected courage. The shelves smell of lavender and clean linen. Her whisper is quick and breathless, and her hands are cold, and grip his sleeve hard.

image.comp: sitting between linen shelves with knees drawn up, leaning into him mid-kiss, trembling with courage
image.setting: narrow linen closet with soft blankets and dim light

jump.goRes: He holds her until the shaking passes, and the kiss turns from courage to comfort, and from comfort to something else.
jump.waitRes: "Not yet." She smiles shakily. "But I would like to sit here a little longer. With you. Quietly."

1.title: Spirited Argument
1.text: Fleurdelys has been shouting about tactics with the security rota for an hour, and Sam, who prefers to avoid conflict, gets caught in it. She turns on him. "You, then. Defend your position." He does, with surprising stubbornness. She stares, then pours two glasses. "Finally. Someone who argues back." Maps curl at the edges under a dagger used as a paperweight. Her wings flare and fold with each retort, a sovereign enjoying a rare worthy opponent.

image.comp: holding two glasses of wine with a challenging, delighted smirk, wings half spread
image.setting: staff room with maps and a heavy table, wine and candles

1.goRes: She clinks the glass, drinks, and kisses him over the rim, like a duel she's glad to lose.
1.waitRes: "Hah! Retreating?" Her smirk is wolfish. "A good general chooses his battlefield. I'll have you on mine soon enough."

2.title: War Room
2.text: Fleurdelys leans over the map of the house and town, planning something absurd. "Every room is a battlefield with better decorations," she says. Sam points out a flaw in her plan. She looks at him a long moment, then slowly grins. "Brilliant. Insolent. Come here." Her hand catches his collar. A lamp throws red light on her wings. She has had two glasses already, and her eyes are bright, her words clipped, her stance a little too relaxed.

image.comp: leaning over a table-sized map with her crimson wings behind her, grinning, hand on his collar
image.setting: back office with a map spread across the table and weapons mounted on the wall

2.goRes: She pulls him in, the map crinkling under their elbows, regal, impatient, and entirely sure of herself until the exact moment she isn't.
2.waitRes: "A tactical pause." She releases his collar with a huff, eyes bright. "I will hold the line. Do not be long."

3.title: Sovereign's Terms
3.text: Fleurdelys receives Sam in her room like an audience. Wings spread, spear stood in the corner, she sits like a throne. "I have commanded nations and fought storms," she says, haughty. "I will have you for a night, and I will set the terms." Beneath the haughty tone, her fingers worry at her sleeve. "...Will you accept them?" The spear leans in the corner, polished and unused. Her voice is crisp and regal, but she has not met his eyes since he sat down.

image.comp: sitting regally in a chair with wings half spread, imperious tone with nervous fingers on her sleeve
image.setting: her room with a spear in the corner, red drapes and candlelight

3.goRes: He accepts. By midnight the terms have been renegotiated, loudly and mutually, and the sovereign is smiling into his shoulder.
3.waitRes: "Not on...?" She blinks, indignant, then barks a laugh. "Fine. Name your own. I will consider them. Briefly."

jump.title: Strong Drink
jump.text: Fleurdelys loses an arm-wrestling bet to Sam by pure cheating on his part (a trick with the bar towel), and she explodes in a roar of laughter. "A scoundrel! I love it!" Then she goes quiet, wings softening, hand still locked in his. "I mean... I like it. Do not read into that." The towel lies crumpled on the wet counter. Her wings tremble, and she is breathing hard from laughing, ruffled and flushed and glorious.

image.comp: wings half-spread and laughing, hands still locked mid arm-wrestle, a sudden blush
image.setting: bar counter with spilled drinks and an upended towel

jump.goRes: She swallows her next retort with his mouth, and when she comes up for air, she is very, very pleased with the defeat.
jump.waitRes: "A draw." Her wings flutter. "Rematch tomorrow. Bring wine, and your best cheating."

1.title: Feng Shui Audit
1.text: Buling is rearranging the fortune-room furniture for the third time this week. "Your chi is sluggish, boss," she announces, shoving a plant. "Because you keep your bed facing the wrong star." She tosses a talisman at him and grins. "I can fix it. Cheap. Introductory price: a kiss." Incense smoke coils around a row of paper charms, and her sleeves are rolled to the elbows. She is flushed from shoving furniture.

image.comp: kneeling beside a pushed-aside plant holding out a paper talisman, cheeky grin
image.setting: small fortune-telling room full of mirrors, paper charms and plants

1.goRes: She plants one on his cheek, then he turns his head and she squeaks and it ends up not on the cheek at all. "Oh! That's a bonus."
1.waitRes: "Pfft. Your loss." She sticks the talisman to his forehead and winks. "The offer is eternal. Mostly."

2.title: Fortune
2.text: Buling reads Sam's palm over a candle with elaborate seriousness. "I see a lucky meeting... a long journey... and..." She pauses, caught on his lifeline. "...oh, no, I see me." Her voice falters. She tries to grin it off. "Spirits are rude. They never warn me when it's personal." The candle flame leans toward their hands. Her patter has run dry for the first time since she arrived, and her thumb is tracing a slow circle.

image.comp: holding his palm over a candle, trying to hide a flustered smile
image.setting: fortune-telling table with a candle, coins and incense smoke

2.goRes: He closes his fingers around hers. For once Buling has no patter. She just looks at him and then leans in.
2.waitRes: "It says..." She snaps her fingers and plays it off. "Come back with a donation and I'll tell you!"

3.title: Lucky Night
3.text: Buling drags Sam up to the roof with a blanket and a bottle. "Tonight the stars are auspicious," she insists. "The lucky hour! Perfect for a big decision." Her swagger has a crack in it. "My big decision is you. Don't make me do the whole fortune-teller speech, it's embarrassing." The air smells of night jasmine and old wood. She keeps tugging the blanket straight, talking too fast, a talisman clutched in her fist.

image.comp: spreading a blanket on a roof beneath the stars, grinning but with a hint of nervous bluster
image.setting: rooftop under a spangle of stars with a lantern and small bottle

3.goRes: She whoops, then goes soft and shy when he reaches for her. Under the lucky stars she turns out to be a very earnest sort of trickster.
3.waitRes: "Pah! The stars are patient." She waves a talisman. "But I'll bribe them. You'll see."

jump.title: Misplaced Talisman
jump.text: Buling is hanging a talisman above Sam's door and wobbles on the stool. He steadies her, hands at her waist. She freezes, mid-nail. "...Wow, that's embarrassing. I'm supposed to be the smooth one." She looks down, red-faced. "Okay, impulse: I'm kissing you now." The hallway smells of paint and pine. The charm swings from its nail, and she keeps smoothing it flat, then smoothing it again.

image.comp: wobbling on a stool with a hammer and talisman, looking down at him, red-faced mid-confession
image.setting: hallway outside Sam's door with a stool and a hanging charm

jump.goRes: She nearly falls off the stool, he catches her, and they both laugh until the kiss resumes.
jump.waitRes: "I'm always careful!" She tumbles down, giggling, and brandishes the hammer. "Just not about you."

1.title: Audit
1.text: Suoming sweeps through the ledger room with a clipboard, finding fault in the second line of every sheet. Sam, the unlucky owner, gets a lecture on tidy bookkeeping. "...Yet, the staff speak well of you," she concedes, tapping her pen. "I find that irritating." For a moment she looks straight at his mouth, then rigidly at the wall. Her pen taps the clipboard in a steady rhythm. Not a single paper in the room is out of place, except for the ones she has just disarranged.

image.comp: clipboard in hand, stern look, eyes darting to his mouth then away, small flush
image.setting: ledger room with shelves of folders and a tidy desk

1.goRes: She huffs, stamps her clipboard against his chest, and kisses him crisply. "Procedural. Do not draw conclusions."
1.waitRes: "A sensible deferral." She makes a note on her clipboard, then crosses it out. "Noted. Reluctantly."

2.title: Two Centuries
2.text: Suoming stops pretending to inspect and sits on the edge of the writing desk. "I have lived two hundred years and watched everything change but myself," she says. "People age past me. I have learned not to attach." A pause. "You are annoying in that you make me forget this." The lamp throws her shadow long against the shelves. She looks young, and that is exactly what troubles her, and she says so by saying nothing.

image.comp: seated on the edge of a desk with her clipboard in her lap, honest and a little lost
image.setting: quiet office at dusk with files and a lamp

2.goRes: She lets him. After a time she turns her palm up and takes the long, slow step she has avoided for a century.
2.waitRes: "No. We don't." She straightens. "But I am considering it. Do not take offense at deliberation."

3.title: Seal Removed
3.text: Suoming comes to Sam's room without the clipboard and without the stern face, looking oddly young. "The seal keeps me looking twenty-five. It does not keep me from being afraid," she says. "I have not let anyone close in a hundred years. I would like to try, once, with you." She sets her jacket down carefully, like a flag lowered. The room is orderly, just as she would leave it. She stands with her heels together and her hands clasped, like a soldier awaiting an order.

image.comp: standing in the doorway without her clipboard, jacket folded in her hands, vulnerable and resolute
image.setting: Sam's room, quiet and tidy with a small lamp

3.goRes: He is as careful as she needs him to be, and she is braver than she expected. At dawn she's already drafted three reasons to stay.
3.waitRes: "I am never unsure." A faint blush. "I am merely... not ready. Wait for me. I am worth the wait."

jump.title: Ministry Review
jump.text: Suoming has discovered a mistake in her own audit and she is furious at herself. Sam finds her hunched over the report, ink on her cheek, shoulders tight. He reaches out and wipes it away. She goes completely still. "...You should not do that." She doesn't pull away. "Do it again." The ink is smeared across her cheekbone, and the room is utterly silent. A moth circles the lamp, and her breath catches in time.

image.comp: hunched over papers with ink on her cheek, looking up at him wide-eyed and frozen
image.setting: ledger room late at night with a dim lamp

jump.goRes: She exhales, pulls him down by the lapel, and kisses him with startling sharpness, then looks horrified and delighted.
jump.waitRes: "I do not take breaks." But she sets down the pen. "...I will take five minutes. Sit with me."

1.title: Blueprint
1.text: Bulma has covered the lounge table with schematics for something she refuses to explain. Sam brings her coffee and she waves him into the seat beside her without looking up. "Genius needs company," she says. "Preferably cute." She finally glances over. "You're blushing, Sam. Good. I'd hate to be the only one." Gears and glass tubes cover the table. A pencil is stuck in her hair, and her smirk is bright and sure, though her cheeks match his.

image.comp: leaning over a table of blueprints with a smirk, one eyebrow raised, hair swept to one side
image.setting: lounge table covered with schematics, coffee and a desk lamp

1.goRes: She laughs into his mouth and says that's the best idea he's had all week. It is, at least, better than the sprinkler system.
1.waitRes: "Ha! Cute and committed." She winks and goes back to the blueprint. "Don't think I won't circle back."

2.title: Prototype
2.text: Bulma proudly presents a rickety lantern that blooms into a hundred little sparks. Hers fizzle. Sam's fingers brush hers as they fix the wiring. "Okay, so I'm usually the smartest person in the room," she says. "But you keep making it interesting." She leans in. "What are you going to do about that?" A warm blue light flickers over her face. A smear of grease marks her jaw, and her tongue is caught between her teeth as she concentrates.

image.comp: holding a sparkling prototype lantern, leaning into him with a bright smirk
image.setting: workshop corner with tools, a spark-lit lantern and open wires

2.goRes: Sparks fly in more than one sense. She is thoroughly, brilliantly curious about everything he does.
2.waitRes: "Pfft. Fine, fine." She waves a screwdriver. "But I'm adding it to the project list. Top priority."

3.title: Night Shift
3.text: Bulma has stayed up three nights with a project and finally flops onto Sam's bed, boots on, hair wild. "I'm brilliant, and I'm tired, and I'm tired of being alone in a bed," she mumbles. One eye opens. "Since I'm already here. Stay?" Papers rustle underfoot. Her hair is sticking out in four directions, and she has the rueful, honest look of someone too tired to bluff.

image.comp: sprawled across a bed with boots on and hair a mess, one eye open with a sleepy grin
image.setting: Sam's bedroom, dim and cozy, a pile of schematics on the floor

3.goRes: He pulls her boots off, and she is suddenly a lot less sleepy.
3.waitRes: "Ugh. Responsible." She curls up, grinning into the pillow. "Fine. But tomorrow, I'm cashing this in."

jump.title: Spark
jump.text: Bulma's gadget explodes in a harmless puff of glitter, leaving them both coughing and laughing in the storeroom. She wipes sparkles from his face, then pauses. "Huh." Her voice is amused, but her gaze lingers on his mouth. "Well. That was unplanned. I like it." Sparkles cling to her hair and lashes. Somewhere behind the crates, a gadget gives a final contented wheeze and dies.

image.comp: covered in glitter and laughing, face close to his, wiping sparkles from his cheek
image.setting: storeroom with scattered gadget parts and drifting glitter

jump.goRes: Glitter ends up in places for days, and she insists it was worth every particle.
jump.waitRes: "Chicken." She grins, unbothered, and flicks glitter at him. "I can wait. I'm brilliant, not patient."

1.title: Rules
1.text: Chi-Chi runs the household like a general and the kitchen like a kingdom. Sam, caught sneaking a pastry, gets a ladle pointed at his nose. "Wash up and sit." He does. She plates him a proper meal, and watches him eat with an unexpectedly soft look. "You're too thin," she says gruffly. "Someone ought to look after you." A kettle sings on the hob and the whole room smells of garlic and ginger. She cooks like she fights, with total commitment and no mercy.

image.comp: holding a ladle with a stern but affectionate expression, watching him eat
image.setting: warm kitchen at night with simmering pots and a lit hearth

1.goRes: She sputters, goes red, and swats him with a dish towel, then kisses him back and pretends she did not.
1.waitRes: "Hmph." She dabs her hands on her apron, flustered. "Then eat the second helping. I'm not giving up."

2.title: Martial Arts
2.text: Chi-Chi teaches Sam a basic stance in the courtyard and corrects his feet with a firm tap. "Straight back. Breathe. No, not like that!" Her hands on his hips, her chin at his shoulder. The lesson stills. "...You're getting better," she says, softer. "I might have to keep you." Dust lifts from the mat as she steps around him. Her apron is tied tighter than it needs to be, and her ears have gone pink.

image.comp: standing behind him adjusting his stance with her hands at his hips, a flushed stern smile
image.setting: courtyard in afternoon sun with a practice mat

2.goRes: She is wonderfully direct. A decisive woman, in all things, she decides quickly and thoroughly.
2.waitRes: "Fine. But posture practice is mandatory." She pats his chest, cheeks pink.

3.title: Homemaker
3.text: Chi-Chi tucks Sam into bed herself, fussing with the blanket, and then, unexpectedly, does not leave. "I've been a mother and a wife and a cook and a teacher," she says slowly. "Nobody asks me what I want." She sits on the bed's edge. "I want to be held tonight. By someone who's grateful." The quilt is tidily folded, as always. She has taken her hair out of its bun, and her hands, usually busy, lie open and still in her lap.

image.comp: sitting at the edge of a bed in an apron, hands twisting in her lap, brave and tender
image.setting: Sam's bedroom with a patchwork quilt and one candle

3.goRes: He holds her. She finally lets the rules go, and the sound she makes is a long, tired, happy sigh.
3.waitRes: "Don't you dare be polite at me." But she squeezes his hand. "Another night, then. I'll bring breakfast."

jump.title: Flour on Her Cheek
jump.text: Chi-Chi has flour all over her cheek and a pie in the oven, and Sam, passing through, gently brushes it off. She goes still. "...Well." Her ladle lowers. "That was forward." Her stern look cracks. "Do it again, and then kiss me, before the pie burns." Steam curls from the oven door. The scent of baking apples fills the room, and her cheeks are rosy, from the heat and from him.

image.comp: wiping flour from her cheek, ladle lowered, a stern look breaking into a smile
image.setting: kitchen with flour dusted counters and a pie baking

jump.goRes: The pie is fine. The kiss is better, and she is enormously pleased with both.
jump.waitRes: "The pie!" She dashes to the oven, red-faced, and spends five minutes avoiding his eyes.

1.title: Taste Test
1.text: Android 21 holds a spoon of Sam's stew out to him, her own eyes half-closed in bliss. "Eleven spices. Three I cannot identify. Do you know how rare that is?" Her voice is breathy, polite, hungry. She sets the spoon down. "I am trying very hard to keep my appetites in order, Sam. You make that difficult." Spice jars line the shelf in alphabetical order. Her eyes are bright, and her voice is polite, but her gaze keeps sliding to his throat.

image.comp: holding a spoon out to him with half-closed eyes, a polite flushed smile and visible hunger
image.setting: bar counter late at night with simmering pots and spice jars

1.goRes: She tastes like cinnamon and something electric. She pulls back, scientific and dazed. "Fascinating. I need a second sample."
1.waitRes: "Understood." She folds her hands neatly, but her eyes follow him. "I will try to be patient. I make no promises about my stomach."

2.title: Research Notes
2.text: Android 21 tallies flavors in a leather notebook at the end of the bar, long fingers curled around the pen. "Subject: Sam. Observation: unusually kind. Hypothesis: delicious." She stops, mortified, and snaps the book closed. "I did not mean the last one aloud. Or at all. Please forget it." Ink-stained fingers hold the pen too tightly. A pot simmers behind her, filling the air with cardamom, and she is plainly distracted.

image.comp: snapping a notebook shut with a mortified blush, polite smile, eyes lingering
image.setting: end of the bar with a notebook, a stack of spice jars, low lantern

2.goRes: She hums, delighted and hungry, and then curious in a manner that is distinctly academic. By the end, the notes are illegible.
2.waitRes: "Of course." Her smile is perfectly polite and a little hungry. "I will update the hypothesis. It will remain the same."

3.title: Appetite
3.text: Android 21 appears at Sam's door with an empty plate and no apology. "I have eaten everything I can. I am still hungry." A faint wry smile. "Not for food. I have tried very hard to ignore this. I am bad at ignoring things I study." She steps in, tall and curvy against the lamplight. "May I stay?" She has put on a tidy cardigan, which makes her look both much more proper and much more nervous. The empty plate shakes just slightly.

image.comp: standing in a doorway holding an empty plate, tall figure in lamplight, wry apologetic smile
image.setting: Sam's room, lamplit, a plate left on the table

3.goRes: She is meticulous, curious, hungry and unfailingly polite. In the morning her notebook has a single entry: 'Satisfactory.'
3.waitRes: "Understood." She sets the plate down neatly. "I will find something else to taste. Do not feel guilty."

jump.title: Midnight Snack
jump.text: Sam catches Android 21 in the pantry at three in the morning, a wheel of cheese under one arm. She stiffens, guilty. "I can explain. Metabolism." The cheese drops. Her gaze moves to his mouth, and her voice gets lower. "...I have an appetite I never explained properly. Would you like me to start with a demonstration?" A single hanging lantern swings overhead. Crumbs speckle her sleeve, and the guilty, hungry curve of her mouth is almost a smile.

image.comp: caught in the pantry with a wheel of cheese, guilty then amused, leaning toward him
image.setting: kitchen pantry with shelves of food and a single hanging lantern

jump.goRes: The cheese is abandoned. She turns out to be a very thorough student.
jump.waitRes: "Tea. Lovely." She picks up the cheese again, composed. "I will bring a knife. We are going to talk about appetites."

1.title: Hair Flip
1.text: Shantae finishes her set on the stage and hops down into the empty hall, hair still swishing. "Whew! Did you see the last spin? I almost took out a lantern." She grins up at Sam, damp with sweat. "You always stay to the end. Nobody does that. You must really like dancing." Her bare feet slap on the polished boards. The lanterns flicker, and her armbands jingle with every breath she takes.

image.comp: grinning with a wild ponytail and flushed cheeks, one hand on his arm, cheerful spark
image.setting: empty stage hall after a show with lanterns burning low

1.goRes: She giggles into the kiss, then whoops and does a pirouette. "Best encore ever!"
1.waitRes: "Aw, no fair!" She pokes his chest, bouncing. "Okay. But I'll keep dancing in your direction."

2.title: Magic Lamp
2.text: Shantae pulls a dented little lamp from her bag and sets it on the bar. "My genie side wants to grant you a wish," she says. "Anything! Free of charge!" Then she notices he is quietly watching her. "...Oh. You're the kind who wishes for something else. Huh." Her ponytail droops pleasantly. The little lamp is dented and wonderfully ordinary, and the faint glitter in the air around her is anything but.

image.comp: sitting on a bar stool with a small lamp, smiling shyly, ponytail drooping
image.setting: bar counter with a dented magic lamp and glimmering bottles

2.goRes: The wish takes a long time, glittery and giggling, and ends in a hush that she has no clever joke for.
2.waitRes: "Okay!" She hops down, cheerful. "I'll hold the wish until you're ready. Genies are patient."

3.title: Dancing Till Dawn
3.text: Shantae dances until the lanterns burn out and the town goes silent. Sam is still there. She stops, breathless, hair damp against her neck. "Okay, I've never been this nervous," she whispers. "I save a town for fun. But this feels scarier." She holds out her hand. "Dance with me? Somewhere private?" Pale gold light touches her hair as the sun begins to rise. Her toes are curled against the cold wood, and her sparkle is a little dimmed by nerves.

image.comp: extending a hand with a breathless smile, ponytail loose, flushed cheeks
image.setting: empty stage hall at dawn, a single lantern left, golden light through a high window

3.goRes: They dance slowly up the stairs, and she laughs the whole way. The night ends softly, full of her warmth and joy.
3.waitRes: "Okay!" She bounces on her toes. "I'll practice. Tomorrow, with extra spin."

jump.title: Impulse Spin
jump.text: Shantae is mid-twirl in the hallway when she crashes into Sam, hair whipping around them both. They tangle and stop, noses almost touching. "Oops!" She's giggling. Then she isn't. "Hey. That wasn't an accident. I might have been aiming." Her bracelets chime softly in the dim hall. A trace of honeysuckle perfume clings to her, and her laughter has gone soft.

image.comp: crashing into his chest mid-spin, giggling, hair whipping around them
image.setting: upstairs hallway with a flickering lantern

jump.goRes: She melts into the kiss with a laugh, then spins them both in a clumsy half-dance.
jump.waitRes: "Ooh, mixed signals!" She grins and boops his nose. "I'll try again. And again. I'm very persistent."

1.title: Plunder
1.text: Risky has been counting the house takings for an hour with a keen, hungry eye. Sam finds her with a small bag of coins. "Don't look at me like that," she says. "It's part of the plan." She tucks it away. "Admit it. You've figured out I'm planning to steal this place, and you still bring me wine." Her coat is slung over the chair, and a pistol-handled quill stands in the inkwell. The candlelight turns her smile into something predatory.

image.comp: leaning back in a chair with a small coin bag and a sly smile, tricorn hat on the table
image.setting: office with a ledger and a candlelit desk, a wine bottle

1.goRes: She laughs, delighted, and kisses him for the audacity. "Pirate's rule: never steal from a man who gives it back."
1.waitRes: "Tch. You drive a hard bargain." She tips her hat with a wink. "I'll steal it in time. The kiss, I mean."

2.title: Treasure Map
2.text: Risky spreads a fake treasure map over Sam's desk. "X marks the spot," she purrs, trailing a finger down it. The finger stops on his chest. "I rigged this, of course. The treasure's right here." She smiles, pleased with herself and a little wicked. "Shall we dig?" The map is tea-stained, deliberately aged. Her rings click on the desk, and she looks pleased with herself and perhaps a little exposed.

image.comp: leaning over the desk with a sly smile, one finger resting on his chest
image.setting: Sam's study with a spread-out map, brandy and candles

2.goRes: She pulls him close, and it turns out the treasure was never gold.
2.waitRes: "Hmph." She smirks, rolling the map. "The treasure will keep. So will I."

3.title: Ship's Quarters
3.text: Risky Boots invites Sam into her cabin, which is just a room with sails hung up on the walls. "I lost my ship," she says, pouring rum. "I haven't lost my taste. I'd like to claim one more prize tonight." She sits on the bed, legs crossed. "Care to be plundered?" Rope and sailcloth hang from the rafters, and the bed is built like a captain's berth. Her bravado wobbles for only a breath.

image.comp: sitting on a bed with legs crossed and a rum glass, mischievous smile
image.setting: her room decked out like a ship's cabin with sails and rope and lantern light

3.goRes: He surrenders with grace. She is a masterful raider, and then, briefly, she is only a woman holding on.
3.waitRes: "Pity." She toasts him with the rum, smiling. "But a pirate knows when to wait for a better tide."

jump.title: Cutthroat
jump.text: Risky traps Sam against the pantry door, one hand braced beside his head, lips curled. "I'll ruin you," she whispers. "I'll outbid you, outwit you, and outlast you." Her voice drops. "I'll start with your mouth." And she kisses him, a challenge and a promise. The door shudders on its hinges, and her spiced perfume overwhelms the pantry's smell of flour. Her eyes burn with challenge and wanting.

image.comp: pinning him against a door with a hand beside his head, wicked grin
image.setting: pantry door in a dim hallway, a lantern behind her

jump.goRes: The kiss is greedy, then startlingly honest. When she breaks away she looks furious at how much she enjoyed it.
jump.waitRes: "Hmph." She steps back, adjusting her coat. "You're lucky I like a challenge."

1.title: Dead Tired
1.text: Rottytops slumps over the bar at dawn, green hair in a mess, grinning from ear to ear. "Dead tired," she says, delighted at her own joke. "Get it? 'Cause I'm a zombie!" Sam laughs. She goes pink. "You laugh at my jokes. Nobody does that." Pale morning light turns her green hair almost gold. Her stitches are visible at the wrist, and she has stopped hiding them around him.

image.comp: slumped over the bar with a wide, tired grin, green hair messy, flushed cheeks
image.setting: bar at dawn with pale light and empty mugs

1.goRes: She tastes like berries and sleep. She gasps, then whoops softly into his shoulder. "Eep! I'm so alive right now!"
1.waitRes: "Aw, bummer." She pats his cheek, bouncing back up. "Okay! Later. I'm so good at later."

2.title: Night Shift
2.text: Rottytops sits on the roof with a legful of stitches, kicking her heels at the stars. "Zombies don't sleep much," she says brightly. "So I get lots of time to think." She looks at Sam. "I think about you a lot. Is that gross? Don't answer that." The roof tiles are cold, and the stars are enormous. Her heels thump the eaves in an uneven rhythm, and her smile slips shy at the edges.

image.comp: sitting on a roof with her legs swinging, bright smile with a shy blush
image.setting: rooftop at night under stars, her legs dangling over the edge

2.goRes: He sits down beside her. She leans in, cheerful and curious and totally unashamed, and the stars get a good long look.
2.waitRes: "Okay!" She hops up, a little wobbly. "That's fine! I just wanted to say it out loud."

3.title: Graveyard Shift
3.text: Rottytops pops her head out from under Sam's bed at midnight. "Surprise! I wanted to ask something and I couldn't wait." She climbs out, cobwebs in her hair, and rests her chin on his mattress. "Can I stay? I don't sleep, but I'm excellent company. And cuddling is, like, a ten out of ten." Dust bunnies cling to her skirts. The bed creaks as she props her chin on it, and her nose is smudged with something suspiciously green.

image.comp: peering over the edge of a bed with cobwebs in her hair, wide hopeful smile
image.setting: Sam's room, moonlit, a scattering of mismatched socks

3.goRes: She curls up warm and green and giggling, and the night gets very interesting very fast.
3.waitRes: "Okay, okay!" She climbs back under the bed. "I'll just be down here. Quietly. Probably."

jump.title: Surprise Kiss
jump.text: Rottytops leaps out from behind a door shouting "Boo!" and Sam doesn't even flinch. She tilts her head. "Huh. You're not scared of me." A grin spreads. "Then how about this?" She grabs his face and plants a big smacking kiss on him. The hall is dark, and her grin is the brightest thing in it. Her heart does not beat, but her cheeks are visibly hot.

image.comp: grabbing his face mid-leap, grinning wildly
image.setting: hallway doorway with a lantern and shadows

jump.goRes: She squeals, hugs him, and spins them both around. "Best scare ever!"
jump.waitRes: "Oops!" She laughs, ears pink. "Okay! Too fast. I'll try slower. Maybe."

1.title: The Doll Shelf
1.text: Sabrina has gone quiet in the lounge, the way she does when the house is too loud in her head. Sam finds her in the back with her small collection of dolls lined up on a shelf. "You have been wondering whether to ask me something for nine days," she says, not turning. "Ask, or I will have to answer it unasked." Rain taps the window. Sabrina has not touched her tea, and the dolls watch with their glass eyes, as if they also know what is about to happen.

image.comp: turning from the doll shelf with one doll in her hands, deadpan expression softening, a faint almost-smile
image.setting: back room with a shelf of dolls, purple lamplight, drawn curtains

1.goRes: Her composure holds for a full second. Then she kisses back, and somewhere in the house a spoon bends itself quietly on a table.
1.waitRes: "Mm. I knew you would say that." A pause. "I did not know it would sting. Interesting." She sets the doll back on its shelf, very carefully.

2.title: Quiet Hands
2.text: Sabrina has been sitting up with Sam through a bad night of rumors and rowdy guests, shielding the whole hall from thoughts that are too loud. At last she sits beside him, takes his hand, and presses her cool fingers into his tense palm. "You are tired in four places. Allow me." She has not said a word about it, but the room is a little warmer than it was, and the candle flame has leaned toward the two of them all on its own.

image.comp: sitting close on a settee, holding his hand in both of hers, calm gaze, a faint flush on her cheeks
image.setting: dim upstairs sitting room, purple curtains, one candle

2.goRes: She finds the knots in his shoulders, then in his breath, then in his nerve. For once the quietest woman in the house does not stop him from hearing her sigh.
2.waitRes: "I decide when I have done enough." She relents, and lets her head rest on his shoulder instead. "...But this is acceptable."

3.title: Nothing Left to Read
3.text: "I cannot read you," Sabrina says at her door, lamp low. "Not truly. You are loud, and then you are not, and I cannot say which is the real you. I have decided that is the reason I want you here. Come in, Sam. Be unreadable. Be mine tonight." She has dimmed every lamp but one and set a pot of plum tea on the sill. Everything about the room says she has planned this carefully, and it is clear she is nervous.

image.comp: standing in her doorway in a plum silk robe, hair loose, steady dark eyes, one hand extended
image.setting: her bedroom, purple silk bedding, a row of dolls on the sill, candlelight

3.goRes: She closes the door with a flick of her mind and then, quite deliberately, with her hand. "Good," she whispers. "No thoughts. Only you."
3.waitRes: "I am never unsure. I am occasionally afraid. This is the second." She smiles thinly. "Take your time. I can wait; I have seen how it ends."

jump.title: All Thoughts at Once
jump.text: The roar in Sabrina's head finally breaks her calm in the kitchen at dusk. She grips the counter, then Sam's collar. "Everyone is thinking about you tonight. Everyone. I would like to be the loudest." She kisses him hard and does not stop at one. Plates rattle on their shelves. A ladle lifts an inch off its hook and settles back, which is as close to a blush as Sabrina's gift ever gets.

image.comp: gripping his collar, eyes closed, composure cracking, flushed, pulling him toward the door
image.setting: kitchen at dusk, copper pots, lamplight

jump.goRes: For once her thoughts and his are the same, and the entire house goes silent around them.
jump.waitRes: She goes still, then nods. "Yes. Breath. A stupid, wonderful idea." She counts four slow ones, still holding his collar.

1.title: A Fascinating Excavation
1.text: Cynthia has spent the week mapping the cellar of the house, convinced a very old wall sits behind the wine racks. Sam finds her dusty to the elbows, a brush in her hand and a smudge on her cheek. "Do you know what I found?" she asks. "Nothing. And I could not be happier. It is the company." She steps closer. A damp, earthy smell hangs in the cellar, and Cynthia's field jacket is draped over a crate. She has never looked less like a champion, or more like herself.

image.comp: kneeling then rising in the cellar with a brush in her hand, dust on her cheek, composed smile and warm eyes, close to him
image.setting: stone cellar lit by a lantern, wine racks, a half-cleared wall

1.goRes: She kisses like she does everything: with attention, patience and no hurry at all. Then, softly, "Fascinating. I'll have to study this further."
1.waitRes: She laughs, a rare real one. "Quite right. A champion with soot on her face. Ask me again at supper."

2.title: Ruins by Lamplight
2.text: Cynthia lays an old map across Sam's desk and lets her hand rest on his. "Legends say two travelers met on a night like this and neither went home." Her tone is academic. Her eyes are not. "I should like to test the hypothesis." Rain beats on the roof. She has brought tea in a travel flask, two mismatched cups, and a surprising number of excuses for staying until the lamp burns low.

image.comp: leaning over a desk with a yellowed map, her hand on his, composed smile with a hint of mischief
image.setting: study lit by a single oil lamp, maps and old books piled high

2.goRes: She is a careful scholar and a patient one. By the end of the evening, the map has gone to the floor and neither of them is reading.
2.waitRes: "Delightful. Then I shall gather more." She rolls up the map, unhurried. "I do not mind waiting. Waiting is most of archaeology."

3.title: The Champion Takes a Night Off
3.text: Cynthia has taken down her hair and put her coat over the chair. At her door she looks like someone who has finally closed a very long book. "I have won every title that I set out to win.
